articles.title: Swansea City: John Toshack watches on as Vitor Matos' table-toppers eye own history
articles.summary: John Toshack and his side of 1981 watch on as Swansea claim their sixth win of the campaign so far, surpassing the previous teams to win top-flight promotion.
articles.body:
Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos says his side have much to do before they start thinking of history, after being inspired by some of the club's greats in his side's comeback win over Norwich City.

Legendary former boss John Toshack was in the stands to watch his former club stay at the top of the Championship, as the Swans fought back to beat the visiting Canaries 2-1.

Joined by members of the 1981 team that won promotion to the top flight – and went on to lead the old First Division until the final few weeks of the following season – Toshack saw Matos' men earn their sixth win from their opening nine games of the campaign.

That is more victories than the now 77-year-old's side mustered over the same period at the start of the season where they reached the top flight.

It is also more than the number of opening wins managed by Brendan Rodgers' play-off winners of 2011, the only other Swansea side to reach the highest division.

Swansea come from behind to stay top of Championship

How Swansea refound their way as ambition returns

Yet while Matos told fans to enjoy the moment as the optimism swirled around the Swansea.com Stadium, he was keen to keep focused on the immediate future rather than making history.

"I have so many things to think about to prepare for games, I don't think about that (the possibility of history)," said Matos, who spoke to Toshack before this first match back after the international break.

"For us the moment is to enjoy of course, but to also have the responsibility that we have a game in a few days [away to Millwall on Tuesday night].

"We can enjoy but not lose focus before the next one. The hardest thing about the Championship is that you do not have a lot of time to celebrate or try to bounce back. You just need to keep going."

Swansea's next two fixtures - against last season's play-off semi-finalists Millwall and promotion favourites West Ham United - are a reminder of that.

But for this challenge against Norwich, Matos suggested there was some inspiration taken by the presence of a side iconic in the Welsh club's identity.

Former Wales and Real Madrid boss Toshack – who also shares a Liverpool connection with former Anfield development coach Matos – was warmly applauded before kick-off, acknowledging supporters from a wheelchair in his first trip to his old club from his home in Spain since becoming seriously ill in 2022.

Asked if if he felt any sense of pressure given Toshack's presence, Matos said: "No the opposite, much more enjoyment and much more honour to be part of a club with this kind of history.

"I think that's always how you need to look to history, it's not a bag that you carry, it's something that you are proud of taking with you and that's what we are doing.

"They know the club much more than me, they leave the club much more than me, I'm here to honour them and to make this a place that they feel as well honoured.

"We have still a lot to arrive there (the Premier League), but it's always nice to be with people who were there."

Despite celebrations after Moussa Yeo and Adam Idah sealed the win over Norwich, Matos reminded fans that Swansea have plenty to do and pointed out that a year ago the side were threatened by relegation.

"I think it's a good feeling, of course, but we know as well that it's a long season," said Matos.

"Even before the game, we were speaking that there's so many games to come. This time last year I was not even here, and in the end we got in some moments really close to a play-off position - so the league can change so much and can drift so much.

"There's still a transfer window in January which can change completely the league again, so we know that's a lot to come.

"But we know as well that our goal is just to focus on the next game and try to be the most competitive team against any opponent."

articles.title: Michigan State incorrectly ruled offside after recovering onside kick in 38-37 loss to Illinois in overtime
articles.summary: The Spartans eventually tied the score to force overtime, but had enough time in regulation to possibly win with a correct call.
articles.body:
An incorrect call on an onside kick deprived Michigan State of an opportunity to drive for a game-tying (or go-ahead) score during the fourth quarter of an eventual 38-37 overtime loss to Illinois at Spartan Stadium on Saturday.

Following a 22-yard touchdown pass from Alessio Milivojevic to Fredrick Moore that cut the Illini's lead to 31-24, Michigan State's Liam Boyd squibbed the ensuing kickoff 15 yards down the right sideline. The ball bounced over the reach of Illinois' Ty Robinson and into the arms of Spartans receiver Samson Gash.

However, the officials called Gash offsides on the play, which negated the onside kick recovery. The ruling could not be reviewed, thus taking the recovery away from Michigan State.

Yet replay showed that Gash was not offsides on the play and the recovery should have been allowed. Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira said on the telecast that he initially thought Gash had gone offsides before Boyd's kick. But after viewing the replay, he said that Michigan State should have been given possession.

The Spartans had to kick again after the offsides call despite the objections of MSU head coach Pat Fitzgerald and the Spartan Stadium video board pausing the replay to show that Gash had not gone offsides. With that element of surprise — and possession of the ball — taken away, the Spartans kicked off to Illinois.

Michigan State's defense gave the offense another opportunity to drive for the tying touchdown, stopping Illinois on a fourth-and-1 from the Illini 33-yard line to get a turnover on downs.

The Spartans then drove to tie the game at 31-31, with receiver Rodney Bullard Jr. recovering his own fumble after an 11-yard gain at the Illinois 2-yard line. Jaziun Patterson followed with a 2-yard TD run and Boyd tied the score with an extra point.

Michigan State's defense once again got a stop, forcing Illinois to punt on its next possession with 20 seconds remaining. Pushed back to their own 33-yard line by a 44-yard Lars Rau punt, the Spartans had little time to move down the field and Patterson was sacked as regulation time expired.

In overtime, Illinois scored on its first play with Michael Clayton II connecting on a 25-yard touchdown pass to Hudson Clement. Michigan State then got a 10-yard rush and 10-yard from Chrishon McCray to move to the 1-yard line. Patterson scored on a 1-yard rush.

Fitzgerald opted to go for a 2-point conversion to win the game. Patterson pitched to Milivojevic on an end-around, and the quarterback's pass to tight end Jayden Savoury was incomplete. Savoury would have been tackled well short of the end zone, anyway.

The incorrect offsides call in the fourth quarter not directly factoring into the game's outcome might be some consolation to Michigan State. But that probably won't be a persuasive argument to Spartans players, coaches and fans.

Gash recovered that onside kick with 7:41 remaining in the fourth quarter. Had MSU drove to tie the game, there likely would have been enough time to try and win the game in regulation. Instead, the Spartans fall to 2-4, 0-3 in the Big Ten, while Illinois escaped Spartan Stadium with its first conference win of the season.

articles.title: Dylan Raiola Benched, Final Box Score Stats from Oregon's Loss to UCLA with Dante Moore Out Injured
articles.summary: No. 13 Oregon couldn't overcome the absence of starting quarterback Dante Moore against No. 21 UCLA on Saturday, falling by the final score of 17-15 at Autzen Stadium.
articles.body:
No. 13 Oregon couldn't overcome the absence of starting quarterback Dante Moore against No. 21 UCLA on Saturday, falling by the final score of 17-15 at Autzen Stadium.

Dylan Raiola served as the Ducks' starter under center while Moore dealt with a concussion , although Raiola was benched in favor of Brock Thomas in the fourth quarter.

Thomas nearly led Oregon to a comeback victory, but head coach Dan Lanning's team ultimately came up short.

UCLA took a 3-0 lead with a field goal on its opening drive, but Oregon gained some momentum after a fumble by Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava on the team's one-yard line.

The Ducks quickly took a 6-3 edge with a short rushing touchdown by Jordon Davison.

Both teams struggled offensively throughout the remainder of the first quarter before UCLA jumped back in front with a 35-yard rushing touchdown by Wayne Knight in the second.

While the Bruins maintained a 10-6 advantage at halftime, Iamaleava was replaced by Ty Dieffenbach to start the second half after suffering an injury .

UCLA's defense was still able to shut down Oregon, however.

The Ducks' three possessions in the third quarter ended with a punt, fumble and interception before Raiola was finally benched after the Bruins took a 17-6 lead in the fourth.

Thomas entered the game and immediately provided a spark to Oregon's offense, as the team went on a 60-yard drive that ended with a field goal.

As the Ducks trailed 17-9, they were able to force a UCLA punt before Thomas connected with Evan Stewart for a 44-yard score.

A game-tying two-point conversion attempt was unsuccessful and allowed the Bruins to keep a 17-15 lead, though.

While the Ducks forced another UCLA punt, they couldn't get into range for a game-winning field goal attempt with 44 seconds left and no timeouts remaining.

Oregon experienced issues with ball security in the defeat, committing seven turnovers. The Ducks also converted a mere one of their 11 opportunities on third down.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 6 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Oklahoma Sooners flipped the College Football Playoff conversation on its head on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners flipped the College Football Playoff conversation on its head on Saturday afternoon.

John Mateer and the Sooners upset the top-ranked Texas Longhorns in Dallas to hand their bitter rival its first loss of the 2026 college football season.

Texas survived a few close calls before Saturday with one-possession wins over the Ohio State Buckeyes and Tennessee Volunteers.

Arch Manning and Co. will drop from the top position in the rankings, but they shouldn't tumble too far because of their previous wins.

Texas isn't out of the CFB Playoff conversation by any stretch of the imagination either, but it needs to improve if it wants to get through a tough SEC schedule with one or two losses.

The Georgia Bulldogs will assume the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 after their win over the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday night.

Alabama likely won't drop far, and it might fall past Texas in Sunday's AP poll because of the nature of the two losses.

The CFB Playoff projection is based off results after Week 6's games.

Oklahoma's last-second field goal knocked Texas from the ranks of the unbeaten.

The Longhorns weren't perfect during their reign as the top team in the country.

After all, they needed a come-from-behind effort in the fourth quarter to beat Ohio State and a strong defensive showing to hold off Tennessee.

Texas is far from perfect, but it still has plenty of talent on its roster to recover from Saturday's loss.

Recovering won't be easy, though, as Texas plays five Top 25 teams in the next five weeks.

That might change if the Florida Gators drop out of Sunday's rankings, but that's still one of the toughest stretches any team will face this season.

Texas could find its way back to No. 1 at some point, but for now, it just has to win game by game to stay alive in the postseason mix.

No. 7 Indiana Survives On The Road At Nebraska

Indiana survived an upset bid in Lincoln in Saturday's early afternoon slate.

The Hoosiers trailed for the first time this season, and for a significant chunk of the game, but they answered the call in the fourth quarter.

Josh Hoover threw a pair of long touchdown passes to Nick Marsh to complete the comeback and keep the reigning national champion undefeated for another week.

Indiana hasn't been in the national spotlight much because it hasn't played a ranked team through six weeks.

That changes in Week 7 when the Hoosiers play host to Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes.

That will be a good barometer of where the Hoosiers stand in the College Football Playoff hierarchy.

Indiana is still on the path to make the playoff, even if it loses to Ohio State, but the game next week in Bloomington will be the test of where it resides in the national title conversation.

No. 13 Oregon, No. 16 Florida Suffer Second Defeats

The Oregon Ducks and Florida Gators have fallen outside the CFB Playoff discussion.

Oregon dropped its second game of the season at home against the UCLA Bruins.

The Ducks already suffered a stunning road loss to the Oklahoma State Cowboys in Week 2.

Florida suffered its second consecutive defeat. It also lost at home in a far more stunning fashion to the South Carolina Gamecocks.

The Ducks and Gators each now have two losses in mid-October, a fate that most teams can't recover from to make the playoff.

Oregon still has to play Ohio State on the road, while Florida has Texas and Georgia to finish out October.

A playoff berth isn't entirely out of the question yet, but both teams to run the table and receive help from elsewhere to be considered in the conversation come November.

No. 2 Georgia Wins On Road At No. 6 Alabama

Georgia will be the No. 1 team in the country on Sunday.

The Bulldogs went into Tuscaloosa and beat Alabama by a 20-17 score.

Gunner Stockton threw for 249 yards, while Dwight Phillips Jr. ran for 120 yards on 17 carries in the victory.

UGA is now the front-runner to win the SEC and one of the favorites to land a first-round bye in the CFB Playoff.

Georgia still has three ranked opponents on its schedule, but only one of them is a true road game at Ole Miss on November 7.

Alabama likely won't drop much in the new AP poll because of the nature of the loss.

The Crimson Tide have to rebound right away on the road against the Tennessee Volunteers next Saturday.

Alabama still has to visit Tennessee and LSU, and if it wins both games, it should easily get into the 12-team field.

articles.title: Arch Manning's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock as No. 1 Texas Gets Upset by Oklahoma
articles.summary: Texas went into the Cotton Bowl on Saturday as the top team in the country, ready to get another win over Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry.
articles.body:
Texas went into the Cotton Bowl on Saturday as the top team in the country, ready to get another win over Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry.

But as has been proven time and time again, rankings mean nothing in a rivalry game.

The Sooners upset Arch Manning and the Longhorns 27-24 on a walk-off field goal.

Texas got on the board first when Arch Manning found Cam Coleman for a 41-yard touchdown.

The Sooners' offense struggled to get going throughout, but they found other ways to score. In the second quarter, it was a blocked punt that helped Oklahoma tie it up.

Texas added another touchdown and a field goal to take a 10-point lead into the halftime, but the Longhorns were far from comfortable heading into the second half.

The Sooners came storming back in the second half, cutting the lead to one score with a field goal in the third before a touchdown drive to open the fourth quarter.

Oklahoma's defense then came through, as Peyton Bowen intercepted Manning's pass and found the end zone to make it a 24-17 game.

After the miscue from Manning gave the Sooners the lead, the quarterback responded well and led a touchdown drive that ended with a pass to Jermain Bishop Jr. to tie things up again.

The Longhorns had a chance to take the lead with just under three minutes to go, but a missed field goal gave the ball back to Oklahoma with the score still tied. The Sooners couldn't capitalize on the miss, though, going three-and-out on the following drive.

But another mistake from Manning gave Oklahoma another chance with less than a minute to play. Manning faced pressure around midfield and tried to find his target, but Courtland Guillory snatched it out of the air.

The Sooners then managed to get the ball into field goal range, and kicker Tate Sandell etched his name into Oklahoma football history.

The upset loss is another stain on Manning's resume amid what has been a rough season. He came into the year as a frontrunner to be drafted first overall, but it's fair to say he hasn't lived up to the hype so far.

Manning had his moments, but two interceptions, including one in the clutch, won't sit well with scouts.

The good news for Manning is that no scouts will be putting John Mateer above him on their draft boards after the way things went on Saturday. Mateer didn't move the ball well at all and was bailed out by his defense and special teams throughout the game.

articles.title: Ohio State Beats Maryland, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock for Jeremiah Smith, Sayin
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes dominated the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday, cruising to a 45-16 win at home.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes dominated the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday, cruising to a 45-16 win at home.

No. 5 Ohio State entered Saturday's matchup as a big 33.5-point favorite over Maryland, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , delivering for Ohio Stadium fans with a 29-point victory.

The Buckeyes offense racked up 449 total yards, but its defense was just as dominant, holding Maryland to a mere 146 yards of offense and 10 first downs.

3. (5) Ohio State: 3-0 (CONF), 5-1 (OVR)

18. Michigan State: 0-3 (CONF), 2-4 (OVR)

Smith, the current favorite in the Heisman Trophy race, leads the pack as the -220 favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . He also leads the Buckeyes all-time in all three major receiving categories: receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns.

Entering Saturday's matchup, Smith led all of college football with nine touchdowns and 823 receiving yards on 44 receptions.

Smith's talent is catching the attention of NFL scouts as he emerges as a top prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class. ESPN's Mel Kiper projected the junior wide receiver as the No. 1 overall pick in his latest mock draft (3:50 mark), placing him ahead of other top prospects, including Darian Mensah, CJ Carr and Trinidad Chambliss.

Ohio State's lopsided win over Maryland further boosted Smith's draft stock, as he added two touchdowns and 93 yards on just four receptions.

Smith's standout performances wouldn't be possible without help from an equally talented quarterback in Sayin, who finished the win over the Terrapins with four touchdown passes and 242 passing yards while completing 62 percent of his attempts.

Sayin is also on the Heisman watch list, though a +3000 underdog to win the award, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The junior entered Saturday throwing for 1,530 yards and 13 touchdowns with just one interception on a hail mary, showcasing impressive efficiency through the first half of the season.

ESPN's Jordan Reid recently ranked Sayin as the 10th-most valuable quarterback prospect, projecting him to be selected late in the second round or early in the third round of the NFL draft.

Ohio State took a commanding 31-10 lead into halftime, scoring on five of its seven first-half possessions.

Smith hauled in two touchdown receptions, covering 33 and 40 yards, adding a flashy one-handed catch to power the Buckeyes' offense.

Sayin also connected with tight end Nate Roberts on a 68-yard touchdown strike, while fellow tight end Mason Williams added to the scoring before the break.

Sayin threw just his second interception of the season in the third quarter, as Maryland's Daniel Wingate returned the pick 52 yards for a touchdown.

Ohio State running back Bo Jackson made up for the mistake on the ensuing possession, capping the third quarter with a 25-yard rushing touchdown to give the Buckeyes a commanding 38-16 lead heading into the final quarter.

Jackson sealed the win with his second rushing touchdown of the game in the fourth quarter.

Ohio State will hit the road next Saturday to face the No. 7 Indiana Hoosiers, with kickoff scheduled for noon ET.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 6
articles.summary: From another classic Red River Rivalry to UCLA winning a rugged Big Ten battle against a contender to the defending national champs getting taken to the brink, this college football weekend provided us with some scintillating showdowns.
articles.body:
From another classic Red River Rivalry to UCLA winning a rugged Big Ten battle against a contender to the defending national champs getting taken to the brink, this college football weekend provided us with some scintillating showdowns.

In the night shift, the Alabama-Georgia game was a classic with a controversial finish, USC took care of business at a Penn State White-Out Game, and Kentucky's run under Will Stein continued with more overtime shenanigans.

And next week's slate is even better on paper.

We've got your winners and losers from the week's action so far. Let's get right to it.

Forget style points. Nothing matters to UCLA besides Saturday's final score, a 17-15 win over Oregon in Eugene.

Now, coach Bob Chesney's team is a shocking 5-0 and the biggest surprise in the nation. Arguably, the No. 21-ranked Bruins will be favored in every remaining game they play.

From out of nowhere to a College Football Playoff team? At this point, you've got to acknowledge Chesney's complete turnaround of this program in Westwood, and the sky is the limit. Remember last year, he took James Madison all the way, too.

The Ducks ended that run, but Chesney's revenge may jump-start this one. Even with Nico Iamaleava leaving the game with an injury and despite three turnovers, UCLA smothered Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola all evening.

UCLA's defense was incredible, forcing seven turnovers and not allowing a single third-down conversion until late in the fourth quarter (1-of-12 in the game). There was no bigger play than stuffing Jordon Davison's would-be, game-tying two-point conversion try after a frantic Oregon comeback late.

It was far from pretty, but that spotless record is, and that's all that mattered.

Chesney has implemented a stout defense and has a star runner in Wayne Knight. It's been enough for a turnaround.

Top-ranked Texas took a tumble against a hated rival once again, somehow losing to Oklahoma 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry.

Despite a miserable start to the season offensively, Oklahoma found a way to cobble together major contributions from all three facets of the game to beat the top-ranked Longhorns.

Arch Manning's second interception of the game driving for what would be the go-ahead score was huge, and John Mateer found Isaiah Satenga III for 13 and 20 yards right after to set up Tate Sandell's game-winning 47-yard field goal with no time left.

For Manning, it's the latest in a line of mixed-bag games that held more bad than good. He also threw a pick-six returned 42 yards by Peyton Bowen for the go-ahead Oklahoma touchdown with 10:07 left. Manning rebounded with a scoring drive, but then threw another huge pick at the end.

For Oklahoma, the defensive score and a blocked punt by Danny Okoye recovered by Dakoda Fields in the end zone for another touchdown helped out an offense that had been sputtering. Mateer did just enough to help supplement a huge win that makes OU 3-2 and sends Texas to its first loss.

"Everybody contributed," a hoarse Brent Venables told the ABC crew after the game. "When we needed to, we made a play."

Lane Kiffin was without a doubt the most-discussed head coaching hire in the country this offseason, but Will Stein may have been the best.

For the second week in a row, the Wildcats went for two in overtime for the win. They got it last week against South Carolina, and they did it again Saturday, shocking No. 10 LSU 35-34 in the extra session. The fans stormed the field, and Big Blue Nation is rolling.

"You gotta play to win," Stein told ESPN after the game, surrounded by a sea of blue. "I don't know what to say."

After CJ Baxter's overtime touchdown, UK first lined up in the "Willie Cat" package with tight end Willie Rodriguez set to take a direct snap. Instead, Stein called timeout and brought quarterback Kenny Minchey back in, spreading out the offense.

With LSU focused on stopping the pass, Stein made a brilliant call with a quarterback draw, and Minchey sprinted untouched into the end zone, setting off the frenzy.

The win moved Kentucky to 5-1 and erased a pair of missed Adam Zouagui field goals in regulation that would have helped the 'Cats win. Zouagui did make a 33-yarder to send the game into overtime, and Stein's play-calling and Minchey's execution did the rest.

Loser: SEC Officiating on the Biggest Stage

There has been a glaring issue with SEC officiating for several years now, and on Saturday night on the conference's biggest stage, there was another colossal gaffe.

With Alabama trailing by three points late in the game, Keelon Russell was throwing into the end zone on a would-be go-ahead drive when KJ Bolden ran into wide receiver Rico Scott early in a play that should have drawn a pass interference call.

There was no call, and on the next play, Bolden sacked Russell to end the drive. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer was visibly irate on the sideline.

Another controversial exchange happened when Georgia got the ball back as an Alabama and UGA player were exchanging words and blows, and the official flagged Dijon Lee for unsportsmanlike conduct and not offsetting flags, allowing the Dawgs to take a knee.

The game was full of heroes on both sides with Dwight Phillips Jr. running for 120 yards for the Dawgs with their top two backs out. Freshman Trae'shawn Brown was a weapon for the Tide, too. Both quarterbacks made plays, and the defenses were stellar.

This was a pair of teams who easily could meet in the SEC title game. It's a shame it couldn't be decided on the field. Instead, huge calls clouded the outcome.

Winner: Indiana's National Champion Response

Curt Cignetti-coached teams simply make championship-caliber plays when they must.

Facing their first loss since December 20, 2024, in front of a deafening Nebraska crowd hungry for a winner and trailing by 11 points in the fourth quarter, Indiana did it again to pull off an improbable 20-17 win in Lincoln.

Josh Hoover first found Nick Marsh for a 75-yard touchdown on a skinny post, immediately answering Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea's 39-yard touchdown run to trim a Cornhuskers lead to four points with 11:51 left.

Then, that duo hooked up again for 44 yards on 4th-and-1 as Marsh went uncovered from a tight formation to put the Hoosiers ahead by the final margin.

"We made a few plays on offense," Cignetti said after the game, and they did, despite only 65 rushing yards.

For Nebraska, it was a squandered opportunity on a national stage that could have given the dormant program its first win over a ranked opponent in 31 tries. Instead, the seventh-ranked Hoosiers continued their incredible run.

Cignetti's team may not be as potent as it was a year ago, but it's unbeaten heading into hosting next week's massive tilt against Ohio State.

After last year's College Football Playoff run, Texas A&M coach Mike Elko spent some money in the transfer portal and attempted to rebuild an Aggies team that lost some weapons.

They obviously didn't do enough with the offense.

Quarterback Marcel Reed is having the type of regression season that South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers experienced a season ago, and the Aggies can't muster enough offense to be an SEC threat. Following a 27-6 loss at Missouri and with a daunting upcoming schedule, they're staring down the barrel of a possible frustrating season.

Right now, A&M is 3-3, and against a resurgent Tigers defense, the Reed-led offense mustered just two first downs and 74 yards through the first three quarters as Mizzou built its lead. They wound up with just seven first downs and 146 total yards.

This is an offense that entered the road game ranked 100th nationally in total offense, and it's going to do nothing but plummet after another atrocious effort. At what point does Elko consider a change at quarterback or shaking things up to find some difference-makers?

Right now, A&M has no offensive answers.

What a difference a couple of weeks make in the SEC.

After demoralizing Ole Miss by 24 points back on September 26, Florida and first-year coach Jon Sumrall were the talk of the country, surging up everybody's rankings and being discussed as a playoff team.

All those accolades sank in the Swamp Saturday with a 38-19 humbling at the hands of a talented-but-struggling South Carolina team that had lost eight SEC games in a row. For the Gators, it was their second consecutive loss following last week's 45-17 road loss to Missouri.

Sumrall's defense obviously has some major issues stopping opponents as LaNorris Sellers had perhaps his best game in two years against the Gators. Perhaps the most stunning thing, though, is just how the Tigers and Gamecocks keyed on stopping running back Jadan Baugh and had success.

When Florida is forced to move the ball through the air, it can't sustain drives, and that has made the Gators look ordinary the past couple of weeks.

Sumrall is seeing that the mess Billy Napier left in Gainesville isn't an overnight fix, and Florida is about to go from the top 10 to unranked in two weeks' time.

On the final play of last week's lopsided win over Cincinnati, Arizona lost leading pass-catcher Tre Spivey for the rest of the season with a broken foot. Rising star Gio Richardson is still out, too.

Even missing their top two receivers, the Wildcats made the difficult, cross-country trip to Morgantown to take on West Virginia, and veteran quarterback Noah Fifita had no issues finding more weapons in dominating the Mountaineers in a 52-31 win.

Nobody is talking about Arizona in the Big 12, but maybe they should be. After dispatching the unbeaten Bearcats and beating WVU this week, they're now 5-1. Fifita makes it all tick, but Brent Brennan has stockpiled some talent in Tucson.

The biggest star Saturday was Isaiah Mizell, whose brother Aidan plays for Florida. He entered the game with just 13 catches on the year but finished with six grabs for 183 yards and two touchdowns, including a sprinting score to put the game out of reach in the fourth quarter.

Brandon Phelps added 88 yards and a score, and with Richardson returning probably next week, Arizona looks like it can score in bunches. Don't sleep on the Wildcats in a wide-open Big 12.

If the No. 22-ranked Houston Cougars are going to be a contender for the Big 12 title this year after losing an early-season close one to Texas Tech, they'll have to run the table in a grueling stretch that started Saturday.

Connor Weigman looked like a steady star leading coach Willie Fritz's team into the "Little Apple" of Manhattan, Kansas, and waltzing out with a convincing 35-16 win over Kansas State in a battle of one-loss teams.

The game was never in question as a team that entered an underdog proved that was ridiculous. Fritz is a proven program-builder, and Year 3 in Houston shouldn't be written off.

But the Cougars are far from home-free. They now return home to host No. 18 Oklahoma State before traveling to Salt Lake City to take on 12th-ranked Utah. Then, it's back home for Cincinnati before ending the season at Colorado, West Virginia and home against Baylor.

Houston needed this win to stay in the Big 12 conversation, and the Cougars took care of business quickly.

A couple wins in a row – including a 31-point, out-of-nowhere triumph over Virginia last week – positioned Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell with the opportunity to take an important step forward and flip the script on a forgettable three-season run.

Instead, Louisville used a second-half smackdown to trounce FSU 44-20 on Friday, overcoming a 14-point deficit to run away with a win behind Isaac Brown's 235 rushing yards and two scores.

FSU fell to 3-3, and with games against Miami, Clemson, Pittsburgh, North Carolina State and Florida remaining, a winning season is no guarantee.

'Noles fans want Norvell – who fell to 4-15 in his past 19 ACC games and 41-37 overall – fired yesterday. But the school would owe him and assistants $68 million if they moved on, is in dire financial straits as an athletic department and in a messy situation with the ACC.

Firing Norvell is certainly no guarantee, but the Louisville loss proved neither is on-field success. The Seminoles are a shadow of their old selves and appear a long ways away from being competitive again.

You're rarely going to be impressed with how Iowa wins, but the Hawkeyes do win. A lot.

After a convincing 41-24 road win over Washington, they're in a prime position for a playoff run. Midway through the season, Iowa sits at 5-1 with just last week's loss to Ohio State.

Quarterback Jeremy Hecklinski completed 12 consecutive passes (three for touchdowns) during an offensive outburst to close the game, and combined with Kamari Moulton's 208 yards, Iowa dominated.

Now, they've got a schedule the rest of the way that probably won't see them underdogs. At Minnesota in two weeks won't be easy, but then they host Wisconsin, travel to Northwestern, host Purdue, head to Illinois and close the season at home against Nebraska.

None of those are gimmies, but if coach Kirk Ferentz's team runs the table, they could be in the Big Ten title game. Even a pair of losses with one being in the championship game could give them a strong enough slate. At this point, you've got to pay attention.

Loser: Pittsburgh Without Mason Heintschel

When Mason Heintschel went down with a season-ending knee injury in last weekend's win at Virginia Tech, Pittsburgh likely knew the victory was bittersweet.

The sophomore was one of college football's unsung weapons, and, behind him, veteran backup Holden Geriner – who had just 21 pass attempts in four seasons at Auburn and Texas State.

Predictably, Geriner wasn't great on Saturday, completing 27 of 44 passes for 219 yards and a pair of touchdowns as Pitt traveled home only to lose to Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Heels, 21-17.

It was the Panthers' first loss this season as they fell to 5-1, and it marked Belichick's biggest collegiate win yet. But the story of this game was just how far Pitt fell without Heintschel.

Coach Pat Narduzzi's program had the perfect playmaker to run Kade Bell's offense in Heintschel, who'd thrown for 1,304 yards, 14 touchdowns and just one interception in a hot start. Now, they've got to find a way to manufacture some offense the rest of the way.

If Game 1 in the post-Heintschel era of this season is any indication, that isn't going to be easy.

Winner: USC's Return to the National Conversation

The past few weeks, USC has drawn the brunt of plenty of national criticism following Desmen Stephens II's egregious hit on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore and subsequent celebration. The defense has been porous, and questions abound about coach Lincoln Riley's job security.

So, getting away from Los Angeles and going across the country to Penn State may have been therapeutic.

It certainly looked that way as the Trojans got well against the Nittany Lions, taking advantage of star freshman receiver Trent Mosley's return from injury to beat PSU in a "White-Out" game, 31-23.

Mosley grabbed nine passes for 111 yards and scored a touchdown as Jayden Maiava distributed the ball around to six pass-catchers – five of which are underclassmen – in a big win.

Coach Gary Patterson's defense had a much better effort against a struggling Nittany Lions offense that continued to reel to 3-3 under first-year coach Matt Campbell. Meanwhile, despite all the noise around USC, the Trojans are now 6-1 and still firmly in the playoff mix.

This is a dangerous team with their weapons.

The 2026 Heisman Trophy race became clearer as Saturday's action unfolded.

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith remains the Heisman favorite and improved his odds by hauling in two touchdown receptions during the No. 5 Buckeyes' 45-16 win over Maryland.

Meanwhile, Texas quarterback Arch Manning's Heisman Trophy hopes took a hit after the No. 1 Longhorns suffered a 27-24 upset loss to Oklahoma.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State: +4000

Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State: +5500

Smith has put together stellar performances on a weekly basis throughout his 2026 campaign and Saturday was no different.

He racked up 93 receiving yards and two scores on just four catches, which included a one-handed grab in the second quarter.

Smith has now amassed 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns in only six games, while the Buckeyes own a 5-1 record as well as a 3-0 mark in the Big Ten.

As for Manning, he had multiple costly turnovers as the Longhorns couldn't emerge victorious in the Red River Rivalry.

Manning finished 19-of-31 for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but he also tossed two interceptions. With the score tied 17-17 early in the fourth quarter, he threw a deep pass that resulted in a pick six.

Although Manning and the Longhorns' offense quickly responded with a 75-yard drive that ended with a touchdown to tie the score at 24, he threw another interception with just under 20 seconds left in the fourth.

The Sooners capitalized on the opportunity, picking up 33 yards in two plays before kicker Tate Sandell connected on a game-winning field goal as time expired.

Texas suffered its first defeat of the season, falling to 4-1.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Oregon and Texas A&M headline the most disappointing teams of the first 6 weeks
articles.summary: Both the Ducks and Aggies lost on Saturday in extremely underwhelming performances.
articles.body:
Somehow, the college football season is nearly half over.

Many teams across the country completed the first half of their 12-game seasons on Saturday. And we've already got a pretty good idea of who is in line for an underwhelming season. Here are our most disappointing teams of the first six weeks, headlined by two teams that were eyeing return trips to the College Football Playoff.

It's incredibly hard to see Oregon as a national title contender. Yes, the Ducks were without Dante Moore, but Saturday's game against UCLA is the perfect example of why you add an experienced quarterback like Dylan Raiola.

Raiola turned the ball over three times and was just 6-of-19 passing for 43 yards before he was replaced by Brock Thomas in the second half. Thanks to a fumble on the final play of the game as Oregon frantically tried to lateral the ball to no avail, the Ducks finished with seven turnovers.

Yet Oregon should have at least had the chance to send the game to overtime. After the Ducks pulled within two on a late fourth-quarter touchdown, UCLA stopped the game-tying 2-point conversion.

Oregon shouldn't have needed to go for 2.

The Ducks only needed that attempt because they failed on a 2-point conversion after their first touchdown of the day. Had Oregon simply kicked the PAT in the first quarter, it would have needed a simple PAT to tie UCLA with 2:16 to go.

That falls squarely on the shoulders of Oregon coach Dan Lanning. Oklahoma State's defense noted that they had cues on Oregon's offensive plays in the Cowboys' Week 2 win over Oregon. This is a roster that has a ton of talent that simply isn't being maximized.

The Aggies' offense is sorely missing former offensive coordinator Collin Klein and receiver KC Concepcion. Klein is now the head coach at his alma mater, Kansas State. Concepcion was a first-round draft pick of the Cleveland Browns.

They were integral to the Aggies' offensive success in 2025. But perhaps we underestimated just how much they mattered. Texas A&M's offense is an absolute mess and had no shot on Saturday in a 27-6 loss at Missouri.

A&M had fewer than 80 yards in the first half and was incredibly fortunate to only trail by seven at halftime. In the second half, the offense wasn't much better until the game was out of reach following Jamal Roberts' game-clinching TD run.

Coach Mike Elko sounded a lot like a broken man in search of an offensive repair guide in his postgame news conference. He opened by saying it was "another extremely disappointing road performance" before responding with this when asked what gives him confidence about his offense's ability to get on track.

"I mean, does this look confident to you?" Elko replied.

He then went on to take a shot at the Aggies fans who are active on the well-known fan site TexAgs.com.

"Again, I mean there's a difference to me between the fan base and social media," Elko said. "And so there's one group that I really don't care much about, [site owner Billy Liucci's] cesspool can go be Billy's cesspool. Our fan base, stay with us. Be behind us. We're going to build something that we told you we're going to build. We're in a really bad spot right now but we'll work our way out of it."

With games remaining against Alabama, Tennessee and Texas, we can safely say the Aggies won't be making back-to-back playoff appearances. And their Week 12 game vs. Oklahoma could be must-see TV if you love offensive offenses.

Another season, another coach, another midseason losing streak.

A year after a three-game losing streak cost James Franklin his job six games into the season, the Nittany Lions are in the exact same spot under new coach Matt Campbell. After beating Marshall, Temple and Buffalo to start the season, Penn State is now 0-3 in Big Ten play after a 31-23 home loss to No. 19 USC on Saturday night.

The loss to the Trojans comes after Penn State was run over by Northwestern's diverse run game in Week 5 and gave up a late touchdown in a Week 4 loss to Wisconsin. This time, the culprit was the USC passing game and the abject lack of a run game.

Trojans QB Jayden Maiava was 21-of-33 for 301 yards and three touchdowns. The USC defense, which had given up 6 yards a play through its first six games, held Penn State to 68 rushing yards on 31 carries as the Nittany Lions were just 2-of-12 on third downs.

If you're looking on the bright side, there are no more ranked teams remaining on Penn State's schedule. But this is also a team that has only played one ranked team through the first half of the season and is still .500. It wouldn't be a shock if Penn State won out, but it's also highly, highly unlikely given this team's deficiencies.

Any reasonable Florida State fan would probably have taken a 3-3 record through the first six games of the season given the Seminoles' schedule. But the way that 3-3 record has happened is cause for some serious disappointment.

In Week 1, the Seminoles forced four SMU turnovers yet still lost on a game-winning field goal. And what unfolded Friday night was even more disastrous than that.

The Seminoles took an early 14-0 lead and had first-and-goal at the Louisville 10-yard line with 10:53 to go before halftime. A three-TD lead was well within reach. Heck, a three-possession lead seemed like a given. Instead, FSU turned the ball over on downs after going for it on fourth down at the Louisville 2-yard line.

And then on the very next play, Louisville running back Isaac Brown did this.

Brown's TD was the first of 35 straight points for the Cardinals as they built their own 21-point lead. After that turnover on downs, Florida State punted the ball on five straight possessions and went three-and-out three times against a Louisville defense that's allowing 5.6 yards a play and is outside the top 100 in scoring defense.

By the way, No. 4 Miami awaits in Week 7.

Things seemed to be lining up for Washington's first Big Ten win of the season Friday night. The Huskies were favored at home and No. 20 Iowa was starting backup QB Jeremy Hecklinski as Hank Brown suffered a shoulder injury in the Hawkeyes' Week 5 loss to Ohio State.

Instead, Iowa opened the game with 27 straight points and Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. left the game with a rib injury and a potential concussion just before halftime. He didn't return in the second half of the Huskies' 41-24 loss.

Williams has powered Washington's offense nearly by himself. In addition to throwing for nearly 1,400 yards, he's the team's second-leading rusher and one of only two players with multiple rushing touchdowns.

Now, Washington — which was ranked No. 17 in the preseason AP Top 25 — faces the prospect of missing their most important player for multiple weeks as simply getting bowl eligible may be the season's ultimate goal. Even with Williams on the field, Washington could be underdogs in at least four of its remaining six games.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Wake Forest: The Demon Deacons should absolutely be in the AP Top 25 on Sunday after moving to 5-1 with a 38-14 win at NC State. QB Gio Lopez is flourishing after his transfer from North Carolina and was 26-of-33 passing for 303 yards and three touchdowns in the win. The Wake Forest defense sacked CJ Bailey three times and held the Wolfpack to 15 rushing yards on 24 carries. Don't be surprised if Wake is 8-1 ahead of a trip to No. 24 SMU on Nov. 14. This is a team that can absolutely make the ACC title game.

Missouri RB Jamal Roberts: The Tigers are letting Roberts eat. A week after he rushed 24 times for 211 yards and three touchdowns in Mizzou's win over Florida, Roberts got even more carries in No. 14 Missouri's 27-6 win over Texas A&M. Roberts had 34 rushes for 222 yards and two touchdowns as he put the game away with a 54-yard run late in the fourth quarter.

Roberts has rushed for at least 125 yards in all but one of Missouri's games against FBS opponents and has gotten at least 22 carries in each of those games. It's a carry rate that may be unsustainable, but it's also working. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight scores through six games.

BYU QB Bear Bachmeier: With star running back LJ Martin out for at least a month, even more of the BYU offense is going to run through Bachmeier. And the Cougars' sophomore QB was up to the task on Friday night. Bachmeier was 22-of-30 passing for 329 yards and two scores while rushing nine times for 109 yards as the No. 8 Cougars beat Iowa State 24-10 to move to 5-0 ahead of a massive game against No. 3 Notre Dame in Week 7.

Florida: The Gators rose dramatically in the rankings and have fallen just as quickly. That's what happen when you lose consecutive games by a combined 47 points. A week after getting blown out at Mizzou, Florida lost 38-19 at home to a South Carolina team that went 1-7 in SEC play in 2025 and was 0-3 in the conference entering Week 6.

There's always a team that comes back to earth after a big September rise, and Florida is clearly that team in 2026. After rushing for 600 yards in Florida's first four games, RB Jadan Baugh followed up his 13-yard day against the Tigers with 59 yards against the Gamecocks. And QB Aaron Philo turned the ball over twice. Games against No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia suddenly look a lot less winnable.

USF coach Brian Hartline: The first-year Bulls coach alluded to UTSA pumping in artificial crowd noise during its home games ahead of his team's game against the Roadrunners Thursday night, saying that he didn't know "how it gets so loud if there's not a lot of people there."

We're guessing that Hartline has now learned to bring things like that up after a game. After his team took a 24-23 lead with 1:56 to go, UTSA went 74 yards in 10 plays as A'Marion Peterson scored the game-winning TD with 15 seconds left for a 31-24 win. The victory dropped USF to 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the American after a Week 6 loss to Temple, while UTSA is now 5-1 and 2-0 in conference play.

West Virginia's defense (again): After the Mountaineers were torched in Week 6 by Iowa State, head coach Rich Rodriguez was exasperated. So was defensive coordinator Zac Alley, who said during his mid-week news conference that he thought his unit was "the worst defense in college football."

Well … there wasn't any improvement on Saturday. Arizona was missing its top three wide receivers and still torched West Virginia for 482 yards in a 52-31 win. QB Noah Fifita was 16-of-23 passing for 341 yards and a touchdown as the Wildcats averaged 9.5 yards a play. West Virginia's offense is really good — the Mountaineers had over 500 yards of offense again — but the defense is doing everything it can to counteract that. The loss dropped the Mountaineers to 3-3 overall and 0-3 in the Big 12.

articles.title: Everything Steve Sarkisian Said After Arch Manning, No. 1 Texas Upset By Oklahoma in Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Steve Sarkisian and Texas were handed their first loss of the season in upset fashion on Saturday as Oklahoma knocked off the top-ranked Longhorns 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry.
articles.body:
Steve Sarkisian and Texas were handed their first loss of the season in upset fashion on Saturday as Oklahoma knocked off the top-ranked Longhorns 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry.

For Sarkisian, the loss came down to making avoidable mistakes.

"You give people chances to hang around in games, and they took advantage of it and ultimately won the game," Sarkisian told reporters after the loss. "For us, there's obviously a level of disappointment. There's a level of anger and frustration because we know we have issues that need to be fixed... But they reared their ugly head today against a quality team."

The Longhorns were penalized eight times for 61 yards and a blocked punt gave the Sooners their first touchdown of the game, continuing a trend of a lack of discipline for Texas.

"I am frustrated. Because we are working at it," Sarkisian said . "It's not for a lack of effort... but it clearly has not been good enough."

Arch Manning threw a pair of interceptions, including one that set up the Sooners' game-winning field goal. The quarterback threw for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but his mistakes were costly.

"Arch competed his tail off and he made some tremendous plays," Sarkisian said.

Execution was certainly an issue, but much of Texas' problems came down to coaching as well. The Longhorns went 3-of-14 on third down, and a decision to kick a field goal on 4th-and-2 late in the fourth quarter came back to haunt the Longhorns when it missed from 53 yards.

But will Sarkisian give up his play-calling duties?

While it's a dissapointing result for a Texas team that has national championship hopes, the Longhorns can rest assured that the loss doesn't have to define their season.

"There's a level of frustration, a level of disappointment, but also a level of optimism knowing we can get those things fixed," Sarkisian told reporters . "We've got a long season to go."

articles.title: Red River chaos: Oklahoma knocks off No. 1 Texas 27-24 on a field goal as time expires after two late Arch Manning interceptions
articles.summary: Oklahoma capitalized on two fourth-quarter interceptions from Texas QB Arch Manning to beat the No. 1 Longhorns 27-24 on a field goal by Tate Sandell as the...
articles.body:
Oklahoma capitalized on two fourth-quarter interceptions from Texas QB Arch Manning to beat the No. 1 Longhorns 27-24 on a field goal by Tate Sandell as the clock hit zero.

The Sooners had the chance to get Sandell in position for the game-winning 47-yard kick thanks to two incredible catches from Isaiah Sategna III after Courtland Guillory intercepted Manning with 19 seconds to go and the game tied at 24-24.

Guillory's pick came as Texas was seemingly setting itself up for a game-winning field goal of its own. Texas had the chance to take the lead with 1:54 to go, but Gianni Spetic's 53-yard field goal attempt sailed just wide right.

Oklahoma punted the ball back to the Longhorns after failing to get a first down. But Guillory's pick gave Oklahoma new life, and Sategna made the most of the opportunity.

The Sooners' top receiver made two fantastic catches along the sidelines to get Sandell into field goal range.

The Sooners' win means that seven of the last 14 meetings between the two teams have been won by the team lower in the AP rankings at the time of the game. Though Texas was favored in 2025, the unranked Longhorns took down the No. 6 Sooners 23-6.

Manning's first interception of the fourth quarter was the first pick 6 of his career. With the game tied at 17-17, Manning sailed a deep pass that was picked off by Peyton Bowen, who returned it 42 yards for a 24-17 lead.

However, Manning and Texas immediately bounced back. The Longhorns needed just seven plays to go 75 yards thanks to a deep pass from Manning to Cam Coleman. Manning then found Jermaine Bishop Jr. for a 15-yard TD to tie the game.

The Sooners' offense has been a mess for most of the season. There was little chance that Oklahoma's offense could keep up without some help from the other units.

And not only did OU get a defensive touchdown, its first score of the game came on a blocked punt, too. Dakoda Fields fell on a blocked punt just milliseconds before he slid out of the back of the end zone to tie the game at 7-7 in the second quarter.

Oklahoma won the game with just 238 yards of total offense. Mateer finished 18-of-26 passing for just 155 yards, and outside of Lloyd Avant's 72 yards, the rest of the OU offense had 11 yards rushing.

The Texas offense continues to underachieve

Look, Oklahoma has a great defense. We're not going to take away anything from that side of the ball. But Texas' offense has looked more pedestrian than spectacular through the first five games of the season.

Sure, some of that is opponent-driven. In addition to OU, Texas has played and beaten Tennessee and Ohio State. But it's hard not to think that Texas hasn't come close to its ceiling on offense.

Manning now has five interceptions in five games, while the run game continues to average less than 4 yards a carry despite the offseason additions of Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers. Manning's connection with Coleman, a transfer from Auburn, is obvious, but Manning is averaging fewer than 8 yards an attempt.

Barring an incredible turnaround in the second half of the season, Manning isn't going to sniff the Heisman in 2026. And both he and Texas' offense will need to be better to get the Longhorns back in the playoff. Though Florida will fall out of the AP Top 25 on Sunday thanks to its loss to South Carolina, Texas' next five games are all against teams that entered Week 6 in the top 17 of the AP poll.

Oklahoma, conversely, could have saved its entire season with the win. Yes, there are serious questions about the offense — and it's impossible to rely on defensive and special teams touchdowns — but the Sooners were assuredly out of the College Football Playoff with a loss to the Longhorns. Now, OU still at least has a fighting chance for another week or more.

articles.title: Penn State Loses to USC, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jayden Maiava, Top Players
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava and USC improved to 6-1 with a 31-23 win over Penn State on the road on Saturday.
articles.body:
Jayden Maiava and USC improved to 6-1 with a 31-23 win over Penn State on the road on Saturday.

While the Trojans have their eyes set on far more, they became bowl eligible with the win. Penn State, meanwhile, dropped to 3-3 as it continues its rebuilding year.

Both offenses came out strong, with USC and Penn State each scoring on their opening drive. The Trojans started with the ball, and Maiava led them down the field before finding Trent Mosley in the end zone. Rocco Becht answered with a touchdown drive capped off by a pass to Andrew Rappleyea.

USC regained the lead in the second when Maiava found Tanook Hines for a touchdown, but the Nittany Lions responded once again, scoring on a short rush from Carson Hansen.

Both teams tacked on field goals in the second, and things were tied up at 17 apiece heading into the break.

A field goal gave Penn State the lead on their opening drive in the third quarter, but the lead didn't last long as USC scored on a rush from King Miller to go up 24-20.

While the Nittany Lions trimmed the deficit to just one point on a field goal early in the fourth, USC once again answered and went up 31-23 on a touchdown pass from Maiava to Kayden Dixon-Wyatt.

After a pair of punts from both teams, Penn State looked to score with just over four minutes remaining, but a crucial mistake quickly killed the drive. Becht completed a pass for what would have been a big gain, but the Trojans forced a fumble to get the ball back.

USC got the ball into Penn State territory, ran the clock down, and left with a win.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin, LSU Stunned By Kentucky in Upset Loss, Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights

articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers were upset in overtime by the Kentucky Wildcats on Saturday night.

Kentucky converted a two-point try in the first period of overtime to knock off the 10th-ranked Tigers 35-34.

The loss dropped LSU to 4-2 and 1-2 in SEC play. Both of those defeats occurred on the road.

Kentucky won the game on a two-point run by quarterback Kenny Minchey in overtime.

The Wildcats got the ball second and scored on a C.J. Baxter rushing touchdown to set up the game's final play.

LSU had the ball first in overtime, scored a touchdown and opted to kick the extra point.

The Tigers only managed to score two touchdowns across the second half and overtime.

LSU pushed ahead in the fourth through a touchdown pass to Roman Mothershed.

Kentucky responded right away with a drive that led to a game-tying field goal with 12 seconds left that sent the game to overtime.

Leavitt produced 275 yards through the air and another 39 yards on the ground in the defeat.

LSU is now 0-2 in true road games under Kiffin, with both of those losses occurring in SEC play.

The Tigers will attempt to rebound at home against the Mississippi State Bulldogs next week.

articles.title: Misery Index: Mike Elko's bizarre rant about Texas A&M fans couldn't come at a worse time
articles.summary: The Aggies got shelled by Missouri and that wasn't even the worst part of the day for the A&M fan base.
articles.body:
Mike Elko is smart — really smart. So smart that long before he became the Texas A&M football coach and landed a $69 million contract, he graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and played on a team that won the Ivy League championship in 1998.

But having a high IQ and a fancy degree doesn't mean you can get away with being the smartest guy in the room. Not when you're in the middle of a disaster season that calls into question whether the football decisions you've made are that smart.

And as the Aggies have descended into a 3-3 funk — hitting a new offensive low in Saturday's 27-6 loss at Missouri — Elko's snark and all his worst impulses are landing like a lead balloon on a fan base that is not in the mood to hear it.

To understand the money quote — the one that's going to haunt Elko until he either starts winning again or gets fired — you need to go deep into the message board culture of college sports, and Texas A&M in particular.

At Texas A&M, the most prominent online gathering place for fans is TexAgs.com, which has grown into an Aggie-centric multimedia company led by Billy Liucci. No matter what you think of the message board (which can certainly be toxic) or the content they put out, Liucci is undeniably the media voice who matters most in College Station. He has been in the middle of the conversation at Texas A&M for nearly 30 years, is more connected than the athletic director and is unapologetic in being an Aggie homer. He was there long before Elko and he'll be there long after.

It might be a stretch to say Liucci can make or break a coach, but he's usually the barometer of which way the wind is blowing.

So when Elko said the following Saturday to a question about fans losing faith in the team, it was a jaw-drop moment: "There's a difference to me between the fan base and social media. So there's one group that I really don't care much about. Billy's cesspool can go be Billy's cesspool. Our fan base, stay with us, be behind us. We're going to build something that we told you we were going to build. So we're in a really bad spot right now, but we'll work our way out of it."

Whatever possessed Elko to say that — frustration, certainly, and probably some arrogance — could be a turning point in his tenure. Even if the heavily online portion of any fan base is the minority, it's not insignificant. Social media may not always be real life, but it is a real place that is part of the experience of being a fan in 2026. Referring to that group of people as a "cesspool" is, to put it mildly, not the best move.

"Going to show restraint here (for now) … but the head coach losing 27-6 then immediately calling out an incredibly large portion of the loyal but also understandably frustrated fan base was a wildly unnecessary misstep," Liucci posted on X.

And he's right. Because at the end of the day, it's not the fans who have lost five out of their last seven games to FBS teams since starting 11-0 last year. It's not the fans who banked everything on quarterback Marcel Reed, who for whatever reason is struggling badly this season. It's not the fans who failed to crack 100 yards of offense against Missouri until midway through the fourth quarter. And it's certainly not the fans who promoted Holmon Wiggins to offensive coordinator this year after Collin Klein left to take the head coaching job at Kansas State.

But they do get to have opinions. That's part of the deal. And if the head coach dismisses those opinions because they're coming from people who don't know as much football as he does, it would be better if he kept that to himself rather than fueling more anger with a fan base that can now be called America's most miserable in Week 6.

ACC: In Friday night's first half, it would have been reasonable to wonder if the worm had finally turned at Florida State. Coming off a dominant win over Virginia, the Seminoles shot out to a 14-0 start over Louisville and were headed down the field once again to seemingly take a three-score lead. But faced with a fourth-and-goal from the 2-yard line, Norvell declined the easy field goal and decided to go for another touchdown. The decision itself wasn't necessarily wrong, even though the screen pass didn't work. Lots of coaches, especially those who come from an analytically minded background, would have done the same. But the real problem is that Florida State immediately imploded, doing almost nothing right for the next two quarters and ultimately losing 44-20. Norvell has been on the hot seat for a couple years and is owed nearly $50 million, complicating the decision for an athletic department that is deep in financial distress. But a team that falls apart at the first sign of adversity like the Seminoles did against Louisville does not reflect well on the culture Norvell is responsible for building. Look, Florida State has some talent issues and isn't one of the top roster spenders in the ACC. But whether it's relying on too many transfers who don't invest themselves into the program or the way Norvell's staff relates to players, it's alarming to see a team that crumbles so easily. The fans have long since had it with this coaching staff, and performances like that may bring the administration along with them.

Big Ten: Was it the missed 40-yard field goal right before the end of the first half? Was it allowing a short pass by Indiana to turn into a 75-yard touchdown immediately after scoring to go up 17-6 early in the fourth quarter? Was it Matt Rhule panicking with 4:40 left after giving up the lead and going for a fourth-and-9 from the wrong side of the 50-yard line? What was the exact moment for Nebraska fans when they felt the dread creeping in, when they knew they had seen this movie too many times before, when a day that was supposed to be the Huskers' big breakthrough turned into a familiar house of horrors? Maybe it was all of them. And while Nebraska's 20-17 loss to the defending national champions was not an embarrassment — if anything, it's proof of concept that the Huskers can climb the Big Ten ladder in Rhule's fourth year — that's little consolation for a fan base that has been battered by so many close calls and disappointments when confronted with similar opportunities. And with it, one of the wildest stats in sports continues. Nebraska hasn't beaten a top-25 team since 2016, a losing streak of 31 games.

Big 12: West Virginia might just retain this spot until its defense gives up fewer than 40 points. The way things are going, it might be awhile. This week's 52-31 loss to Arizona in Morgantown was another defensive disgrace, with Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita lighting them up for 482 yards. But what's even more demoralizing for West Virginia is that it actually outgained Arizona with 522 yards only to get blown out thanks to touchdown drives of 58 seconds and 49 seconds early in the fourth quarter. Afterward, coach Rich Rodriguez said it's as "frustrated as I've ever been defensively," and he should be after West Virginia lost a game for the second time in program history after rushing for more than 300 yards with 30-plus first downs. "I don't blame the fans for being upset when the guy just hands the ball off and one guy's out of a gap and he runs for 60 yards," Rodriguez said. "Well, where's everybody else at? Does that mean there's 10 other guys that can't rally to the ball or whatever? It's ridiculous. … You can't win playing that poorly on defense." No, you can't, and West Virginia could be headed for a second straight basement-adjacent finish in the Big 12 if it's not fixed.

Group of Six: Few programs have grown in stature in the last decade more than Tulane, which broke out of its long cycle of losing to make the Cotton Bowl in 2022 and the College Football Playoff last season. But any program that aspires to a permanent place among the Group of Six elite will inevitably have to nail multiple coaching hires in a row to stay there. Anyone can luck their way into one good coach. It's a lot harder to do it twice. But a third time? Good luck. Tulane certainly got it right with Willie Fritz (now at Houston) and Jon Sumrall (now at Florida). The third hire, however, was Tulane's sustainability check — and athletic director David Harris might have misfired with Will Hall, who dropped to 2-3 after a 20-17 loss to Army. If Hall doesn't ultimately work out, it will be an even bigger problem than normal for Harris. That's because Hall already had a track record at the FBS level. It wasn't a good one, posting a 14-30 record at Southern Miss before being fired midway through the 2024 season. It's hard to get fired in college football and land a better job less than two years later. Maybe there's a reason for that.

Steve Sarkisian: Oklahoma-Texas is the best rivalry in college football because you'd have a better chance of flipping a coin to pick the winner than relying on the way either team has played leading into the game. There's just something about the long history of that game, the intensity of hate built up over time between the two fan bases and the truly neutral field at the Cotton Bowl that makes it special. "Throw out the record books" is a cliché that doesn't usually hold up when one team is clearly better than another, but the Red River Rivalry almost never goes the way you think it will. And that makes the pain for Sarkisian this year so much greater because, by all the ways we measure football teams, the Longhorns are significantly better than Oklahoma. In fact, the narrative around the Sooners was getting ugly after a September in which their offense looked completely broken. After a 41-13 loss to Georgia, what possible path did they have to beat a No. 1-ranked Texas team with a win over Ohio State? Well, we all saw it Saturday as Tate Sandell nailed a 47-yard field goal as time expired for a stunning 27-24 win . Though this loss doesn't kill Texas' playoff hopes, it does raise a lot of questions. Because outside of the fourth quarter against the Buckeyes, Texas hasn't played to its immense potential at any point this season — a trend that has emerged an awful lot in Sarkisian's career. If this team with Arch Manning at quarterback, a truly elite defense and NFL-level talent everywhere can't win a title, will it ever happen for him?

Dan Lanning: There are a handful of coaches who have been convinced that it's analytically sound to go for two after a touchdown early in the game, and Lanning has done it many times. But when it comes back to bite you, it bites you hard. Though it wasn't the only reason or even the primary reason Oregon lost to UCLA, 17-15 , not converting turned out to be a crucial swing by the end. Because when Oregon finally got in the end zone again with 2:16 left, it forced the Ducks to go for two rather than kick an extra point to tie. And when they didn't get it (yet again), the Bruins had a program-defining victory and Oregon was left with a second loss that puts its CFP hopes on the brink. Moreover, the way Oregon played offensively throughout this game should raise some questions about the entire operation. Are the Ducks really so reliant on quarterback Dante Moore, who was out with a concussion, that they can't do anything without him? Oregon had just 272 yards of offense and a stunning seven turnovers while turning to third-stringer Brock Thomas after Dylan Raiola struggled badly. For the first time in Lanning's tenure, Oregon fans have reason to be worried about the trajectory.

Brent Pry: A year ago at this time, Pry was free. After 40 games as Virginia Tech's head coach, he was living the buyout life and was no longer the subject of weekly calls for his job by a fan base that had long since lost its patience for mediocrity. But lo and behold, he's given Hokies fans reason to demand his firing for a second time by agreeing to return as defensive coordinator under James Franklin. Though you could argue that offense was the biggest culprit in Virginia Tech's 25-20 loss at Cal, Pry's defense had a chance to win the game after the Hokies scored with 1:15 left to finally take the lead. Instead, Virginia Tech immediately handed Cal 30 yards on consecutive plays with a roughing the passer call and a pass interference penalty, followed by a 31-yard pass play to set up the winning touchdown with 18 seconds left. Though the second penalty was shaky — officials could have easily called it the other way — you can't let that happen against a Cal team that was missing star quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele due to a concussion and has been a mess on offense all season.

Jedd Fisch: The Washington Huskies have never looked more miscast as a Big Ten team than they did Friday night in a 41-24 Seattle shellacking at the hands of Iowa. At 3-3, Washington is arguably the most disappointing team in the country at the halfway mark after starting with a top-20 preseason ranking. Remember the offseason drama with quarterback Demond Williams, who tried to enter the transfer portal days after signing a big deal with Washington, only to back down once it became clear the school was going to do whatever it could to legally enforce the contract? Well, that's backfired on everyone. Williams hasn't played too well, and when fans see Washington on the field against a well-oiled machine like Iowa, there's a stark difference in who's more physical and more together as a program. Washington is not a top-half spender in the Big Ten, and there are some questions in the industry about how committed the university really is to its football product, but the Huskies should not be nearly this bad in Fisch's third season.

A South Florida stumble: First-time head coaches usually have a lot to learn. But after playing and coaching football their whole life, they should already know one of the fundamental truisms across all sports: Don't poke the bear. And when South Florida's new coach Brian Hartline suggested at his weekly press conference that UTSA pumps noise into the Alamodome to create a home-field advantage, consider the bear poked. The bear, in this case, was UTSA coach Jeff Traylor, one of the saltiest hardboots in college coaching. And when he heard the following quote — "I've heard it's really loud there. Trying to figure out what the population size is, you know, I don't know how it gets so loud if there's not a lot of people there," Hartline said — Traylor had all the fuel he needed for a 31-24 win in front of a crowd that harangued Hartline all night. It was just a complete whiff by Hartline, the longtime Ohio State assistant, because other coaches have made the same accusation before and gotten similar results. UTSA's home environment has been the most notable thing about the program — they're 36-5 under Traylor in the Alamodome and care deeply about it — so poking at that sore spot earned Hartline the loss he deserved.

Arkansas' head-scratcher: Razorback fans have been in "fire everybody" mode the entire season. They want athletic director Hunter Yurachek gone and don't believe Ryan Silverfield, who Yurachek hired away from Memphis, has the coaching chops to survive in the SEC. Though Arkansas' problems go way deeper than the head coaching position, Silverfield did himself no favors in a 24-17 loss to Tennessee when he punted the ball away with 1:45 left and never got it back. Though Arkansas had all three timeouts remaining, it's an easy one to second-guess with that little time on the clock and with a team that has little to lose at this point in the season. Did Silverfield think they really had a better chance of stopping Tennessee on three straight plays, then driving again with a minute or so on the clock, as opposed to making 10 yards on one play to keep the drive alive? "I think a fourth-and-10 percentage for us, especially the way we were protecting at the end, probably was under 5 percent chance to get it," Silverfield said. Sorry, but if you're going to lose the game, lose it because you tried to make a play.

Kennesaw's (bad) karma: Kennesaw State was one of the fun stories of last season, winning the Conference USA title and going 10-4 under first-year coach Jerry Mack, who got some buzz for bigger jobs. This year? Not so fun. The Owls are 1-4 after a 27-26 loss at home to Jacksonville State, but the important context is how they lost this game on Wednesday night. In a one-point game, Kennesaw State missed an extra point in the second quarter, blew a nine-point lead early in the third quarter, appeared to rescue the game with a field goal for a 26-24 lead with 2:15 left and then gave up an 11-play drive in 83 seconds, resulting in Jacksonville State's game-winning field goal.

articles.title: El Madrid no juega, pero agita
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Mourinho no da con el equipo, pero a cambio se ha agarrado gozoso a la cuerda victimista que él mismo instaló en el Madrid y que ahora le viene de perlas para que la falta de juego pase a un segundo plano. Y encima, como al que nace para martillo, los clavos le caen del cielo. Ayer ocurrió una jugada como inventada por el diablo, que transformó un gol de Vinicius en expulsión del propio Vinicius, nada a menos, VAR mediante. En el arranque de la jugada Saliba quiso obstruirle y él se lo quitó de delante con un tirón de pelo, acción que el reglamento sanciona con roja (conducta violenta), aunque no mucha gente lo sabe, porque es una jugada que se da poco. Pero se da y se resuelve con expulsión... desde hace cuatro años. Así que es ocioso esgrimir casos anteriores (la pasó a Marcelo ante el Alavés en el Di Stéfano durante la pandemia) porque hay varios precedentes ya de la aplicación de esta norma y ayer mismo le pasó a Athenea del Castillo en Estados Unidos con la selección. Eso dio paso a un tramo final de partido bronco y feo, tarjeta va tarjeta viene, con Mourinho de sumo sacerdote farmeando aura de lo lindo para excitación de los excitables. Por cierto, Vinicius, que vio el primer tiempo desde el banquillo, estaba jugando bien, agitando el ataque del Madrid y mejorando mucho la primera parte de Diomande, que tras la salida del brasileño pasó a la banda derecha, donde cazó, a buen pase de Valverde, el gol del partido, con un remate cruzado de perfecta ortodoxia, remediando así su flojo primer tiempo. Güler fue con mucho el mejor del Madrid, Bellingham sólo apareció muy al final parta hacerse dueño del balón en los histéricos minutos del descuento y Mbappé se trabajó tres ocasiones, pero no consiguió marcar. El Villarreal mostró orden y timidez en la primera parte y algo más de atrevimiento en la segunda, pero sus remates, que tampoco fueron muchos, toparon con Courtois. En definitiva, puntos salvados por el Madrid, más madera para la queja arbitral y muy probable baja de Vinicius para el Clásico.
