articles.title: Martín Presa lo tiene claro; Peter Lim, no
articles.summary: Sin ataduras
articles.body: No se puede continuar como propietario de un club si una afición no quiere. Si la masa social: la de abonados y la de simpatizantes que van ocasionalmente al campo, se plantan ante el propietario, eso acaba antes o después con la salida del propietario, vendiendo sus acciones. Ayer se suspendió el partido del Rayo-Athletic porque su afición dejó claro que no quiere a su propietario. No entro en los detalles; simplemente describo hechos evidentes. La afición de Vallecas fue ingeniosa para poner un palo en la rueda de la bicicleta. Sin violencia, con ingenio: aviones de papel y bolas de papel o de plástico de colores. El partido se tuvo que detener por dos veces y ser suspendido finalmente. Martín Presa tiene un problema. Ya lo sabía que lo tenía porque ha habido hechos pasados que se lo han ido dejando claro. Pero lo de ayer es un antes y un después porque le han enseñado como pueden hacer imposible la vida normal del equipo si él sigue o si no cambia el rumbo hacia la dirección que sus aficionados quieren (repito que no entro hoy en el fondo del asunto). Los aficionados del Rayo están tan hartos que no se han parado a pensar si con la suspensión del partido perjudican a su equipo por si le pudieran quitar puntos u otras sanciones. Han pensado que motivo mayor tapa a justificación menor. Presa no puede seguir al frente del Rayo, si sabe que cuando se descuide le van a destrozar el palco por la noche, o le van a detener un partido en juego hasta hacer que se suspenda. Otro día evitarán que llegue el autobús al partido, se quedarán en calzoncillos todos en el campo… o vete tú a saber. Pero Presa ya tiene una inseguridad que le hará estar pensando si ha llegado el momento de irse del Rayo y poner en venta su paquete accionarial del 98%. Y no creo que tuviese problemas en encontrar un comprador con facilidad dada la escasa o nula deuda, una masa de abonados de 13.000 y le faltará un proyecto de remodelación o nuevo estadio. Los aficionados de la Lazio han tomado una primera medida que es vaciar el estadio hasta que el dueño Lotito se vaya y venda el club. No se han parado a buscarse excusas de que no yendo al estadio perjudican al equipo, o que su rechazo a Lotito no va a hacer que se separen de su sentimiento por el Lazio. No se han fabricado una autoexcusa de “a mi Lotito no me va a echar de mi estadio”. No conformes con eso, iniciaron una campaña para no hacerse el abono de temporada y ha habido bajas de casi un 90 %. Han bajado de 30.000 a 4.000. Sin embargo posiblemente Peter Lim pueda tener dudas de si realmente es cierto que no le quieren en Valencia. Conozco perfectamente toda la campaña Lim Go Home, las banderitas amarillas, el cántico fugaz del minuto 19 de Lim Go Home…etc. Pero Peter Lim no ha sufrido ningún guantazo social potente después de 12 años como propietario del Valencia CF. Nunca han conseguido vaciar Mestalla en una protesta contra él. Cuando se ha intentado no se ha conseguido; e incluso se ha fracturado la afición quedándose en un partido contra el Girona, la mitad dentro y la mitad fuera: acabaron insultándose y protestando los unos contra los otros. Eran tiempos de miedo en el equipo (como viene sucediendo las últimas temporadas) porque flirteaba con el descenso deambulando por los últimos puestos. Cuando más hartazgo había de Lim en junio de 2024 ocurrió una cosa increíble en Valencia: el PP- el PSOE y Compromís (versión valenciana de Podemos) se pusieron de acuerdo para votar a favor de devolverle a Peter Lim los beneficios urbanísticos que había perdido por su incumplimiento grave y recalcitrante. Cuando Lim compró el Valencia en 2014 sabía que había un contrato con el Gobierno autonómico y local por el que debía finalizar e inaugurar el Nuevo Mestalla que estaba a medio acabar antes de mayo de 2021 o perdería los permisos urbanísticos que le había regalado la Administración para que en el solar del actual estadio de Mestalla (una vez derribado) se pudiesen construir y vender 600 pisos de lujo y un gran centro comercial. Ambas cosas suponen un valor para el Valencia cuando venda ese solar con ese permiso de entre 150 y 170 millones de euros. Lim incumplió y el Gobierno del PSOE y Compromís de la Generalitat Valenciana ,fue forzado legalmente por asociaciones locales a que se caducara el acuerdo. Era un momento ideal para forzar a Lim desde la política con un mensaje claro que simbólicamente sería : “Usted en Valencia ya no tiene nada más que hacer. No le queremos. Ya no hay más leche en la teta de la vaca. Venda la vaca y váyase“. Sin embargo apareció en el horizonte el Mundial 2030 y el señuelo o el anzuelo de ser sede de algún partido del Mundial 2030 ( ya veremos lo que pasa al final ). Y entonces ocurrió una traición desde lo más profundo de la política: los 13 concejales del PP con la actual alcaldesa María José Catalá al frente, los 9 de Compromís y los 7 del PSOE votaron a favor de renovarle y devolverle el diamante de 150-170 millones a Lim a cambio de que acabará en Junio de 2027 es Nuevo Mestalla que debió acabar en mayo de 2021. Ya saben que en España no se ponen de acuerdo el PSOE, Compromís y el PP ni en los desahucios; pero se pusieron de acuerdo para engordarle los bolsillos a Peter Lim y para alargarle la agonía a los aficionados. Ahora cuando Lim algún día ponga a la venta sus acciones, pedirá más dinero por ellas porque su 95% vale más con el campo nuevo acabado. Los políticos dirán que han acabado con un problema enquistado desde 2009 cuando se detuvieron las obras del estadio por la grave situación económica del club en aquellos años. Los 29 concejales no entendieron que la sociedad pedía acabar con Peter Lim antes que acabar el Nuevo Estadio. Ese era el mandato social a gritos. No vale la excusa fácil de que la culpa es de los políticos, porque si los políticos le tuviesen miedo o respeto a la gente del valencianismo no lo habrían hecho. Pero al valencianismo le ha perdido el respeto sus propios políticos y por supuesto Peter Lim. Sin embargo he de decir que después de eso y pese a que la gente es evidente que quiere que haya un cambio de propietario, la realidad es que cada año hay más abonados, que los asientos son más caros que en época de Champions y que hay más abonados ahora que la última vez que el equipo jugó la Champions. Por tanto hasta los políticos podrían pensar que actuaron bien. Hace menos de un mes, se había activado de nuevo el vaciado del estadio. Parecía que iba en serio conseguirlo por primera vez. El grupo organizado Curva Nord había vaciado sus localidades en el fondo en el partido anterior, sin que le siguieran los demás. Pero los dos grupos más fuertes sociales del valencianismo (Libertad VCF y Curva Nord) habían coincidido en vaciar Mestalla en el partido ante la Real Sociedad del pasado 20 de septiembre. Todo estaba convocado. Los carteles puestos. Pero 4 días antes, echaron a Corberán y al medio jubilado Ron Gurlay, ficharon a Braulio y a Aguirre y el vaciado se desactivó y se canceló. Facilito y rapidito… pensaría Peter Lim. Para más contradicción, el hijo de Peter Lim, que responde al nombre de Kiat y es el presidente del club, tuvo el atrevimiento y valentía de asistir y presidir el palco el 6 de septiembre en el partido ante el Barca. No me digan cómo sucedió pero Kiat Lim sonreía en el palco y ese día le pitaron más a Gayá que a Kiat Lim. Añadan que el club se ha visto obligado a cerrar la lista para nuevos abonados en el Nuevo Estadio para la 27/28. Actualmente el club tiene 40.000 abonados y han cerrado la lista para el Nuevo Estadio en 52.000. Para sacar sus propias conclusiones, metan en el análisis la ilusión por ir al Nuevo Estadio (hay mucha contestación social por el proyecto final) y metan también el hartazgo con el nivel deportivo del equipo que se ha vulgarizado. Mezclado todo salen 12 abonados más de los 40.000 abonados a un Valencia CF actual vulgar que lleva varias temporadas luchando por no descender muchas jornadas. Por todo lo anterior entendería que Peter Lim tenga dudas de que realmente no le quieren en Valencia. Siendo un hombre abstraído de las noticias y habiendo un enorme embudo a su alrededor para que le llegue poca información, no me extrañaría que piense mirando los hechos y los datos objetivos que es mentira que no le quieran. Sin embargo yo creo que Martín Prensa y Lotito tienen claro que lo van a tener muy difícil, antes o después, para seguir al frente de sus clubes y no poner en venta su paquete accionarial. Añadan que Lim vive en Singapur y no viene por Valencia (casi) nunca. Sin embargo si sucedieran cosas parecidas a las que pasan en el Rayo y en la Lazio, seguramente sabría que tiene un problema serio de verdad, como lo tienen los otros dos. Y se vería urgido a buscar una solución. Postdata: Tengo claro que habiendo seguramente más motivos en Valencia que en Vallecas o en Roma (Lazio) en Mestalla no sucederá nada que a Lim le mueva las carnes y haga que no siga viendo plácidamente, en su casa con los pies en la mesa, la película ‘El Silencio de los Corderos’.

articles.title: La 'explosión' de Vallecas
articles.standfirst: Los aficionados del Rayo Vallecano protestaron contra la directiva y el partido se suspendió por lanzamientos de objetos al campo. El club se sigue 'fracturando'
articles.summary: Los aficionados del Rayo Vallecano protestaron contra la directiva y el partido se suspendió por lanzamientos de objetos al campo. El club se sigue 'fracturando'
articles.body: Y al final Vallecas explotó. La vuelta de LaLiga al barrio no fue como muchos aficionados se esperaban (sobre todo por aquellos desplazados del Athletic Club para ver a su equipo), pero sí como la mayoría de Rayistas querían. El partido entre el Rayo Vallecano y el Athletic Club quedó suspendido cuando habían pasado 52 minutos del inicio de un duelo que se tuvo que detener hasta en tres ocasiones. Los motivos fueron una lluvia de aviones de papel y de pelotas de "aproximadamente dos centímetros de diámetro", según recoge el acta arbitral, como medida de protesta contra el presidente Raúl Martín Presa. Ya en la rueda de prensa del viernes por la tarde, convocada por la Agrupación de Peñas del Rayo Vallecano, se avisó de que en este primer partido se iba a protestar de forma pacífica, pero en aquel momento nadie vislumbraba lo que ocurriría al día siguiente. Las fachadas del estadio amanecieron con carteles de 'S.O.S Rayo' y a varias horas del comienzo del encuentro se repartió una hoja titulada: "Es el día de protestar. Es el día de señalar a Presa". En ella aparece un texto en el que se pide a todo el Rayismo "que convierta el descontento en rabia" y que lo exprese de la siguiente forma y con determinadas instrucciones. "Minuto 1: Pitada contra el palco. Minuto 13: Bufandeo y cánticos contra el palco. Levanta tu bufanda de 'Presa Vete Ya' y que el ruido ambiente se cuele en todas las emisoras. Cuando acabe el minuto 13: Haz un avión con este panfleto". Al himno de 'So Payaso', 'La Vereda de la Puerta de Atrás' o 'El Vals del Obrero' comenzaron los protagonistas a calentar. Pero ni con música, se calmaban los ánimos de una afición que comenzó con los pitos contra su presidente antes del inicio del encuentro, con él todavía ausente del palco presidencial. En el minuto 1 comenzaron los abucheos, pero el encuentro transcurrió con normalidad. La afición hasta celebró un gol de Jorge De Frutos que acabó siendo anulado por fuera de juego inicial de Sergio Camello. El Rayo salió bien al encuentro, pero cuando transcurría el minuto 13 y el Athletic iba a lanzar un córner en ese fondo sur, una lluvia de aviones de papel y de pelotas de pequeñas dimensiones irrumpió en el campo. Inmediatamente, José María Sánchez Martínez detuvo el juego y mandó a los jugadores a la banda. Activó el “Protocolo 1”. Las gradas desplegaron sus bufandas en contra de la presidencia, mientras que al césped entraron los operarios para recoger los objetos lanzados. Los jugadores del Rayo Vallecano les ayudaron para despejar el césped y también se vio a algún jugador del Athletic ayudando como Aitor Paredes. Los demás se mantenían escuchando las instrucciones de sus entrenadores y viendo una escena que es rara verla en España. En Alemania ya han ocurrido varias lluvias de pelotas de tenis como forma de protesta, pues en Vallecas fueron los aviones de papel y las pelotas de goma. A las 14:25, una vez se retiraron la mayoría de los objetos que lanzaron al césped, se reanudó el encuentro. Tan solo se sacó el córner cuando se volvieron a tirar cosas desde ese fondo sur y los jugadores se marcharon a los vestuarios directamente por orden del colegiado. Se inició el “Protocolo 2”. La situación en Vallecas fue límite y los aficionados siguieron mostrando su descontento. Mientras que las autoridades presidenciales se retiraron hacia dentro del estadio. Los capitanes, Isi y Óscar Valentín, salieron a hablar con los aficionados del fondo sur. Por megafonía anunciaron que en diez minutos saldrían los jugadores a calentar y que cinco después se reanudaría el encuentro. Además, también se comunicó que si persistía el lanzamiento de objetos, el encuentro se suspendería definitivamente. A las 14:42, el encuentro se reanudó, pero tan sólo duró medio minuto el juego. Se volvieron a lanzar objetos y Sánchez Martínez volvió a detener el encuentro. Durante esta detención, el colegiado habló con los entrenadores, los capitanes y los cuerpos de seguridad. “Tras este último incidente, la Coordinadora de Seguridad de la Policía Nacional nos comunicó que debíamos proceder a la suspensión definitiva del partido, al no poder garantizarse las condiciones de seguridad necesarias para la continuación del encuentro", recogió Sánchez Martínez en el acta. Poco a poco los aficionados fueron desalojando el estadio y algunos hinchas del Athletic preguntaron en las taquillas rayistas para saber cuál era el procedimiento que debían seguir para la devolución del dinero. “No perdáis la entrada” afirmaron los trabajadores. El Athletic anunció que “contactará con los athleticzales que hayan adquirido sus localidades a través del club para gestionar su devolución”. Varios jugadores rayistas se acercaron a hacerse fotos y firmar a la afición como Unai López, Dani Cárdenas, Unai López o Pathé Ciss. Sin embargo, ninguno hizo declaraciones. El primero en hacerlas fue Óscar Valentín por medio de un mensaje por su red social ‘X’ en el que expresó la necesidad de “una vía de acercamiento entre todas las partes, poniendo siempre por delante el bien común y, sobre todo, el bien del Rayo Vallecano”. La Agrupación de Peñas del Rayo Vallecano también compartió un mensaje. “Lo sucedido hoy durante el partido frente al Athletic Club es el reflejo inevitable del hartazgo, la frustración y el enfado de miles de abonados tras años de nefasta gestión por parte de Raúl Martín Presa”, rezaba el comienzo del comunicado. Quien condenó la situación fue el Consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte, Mariano de Paco Serrano, también por su red social ‘X’. Desde la Comunidad de Madrid condenamos lo ocurrido hoy en Vallecas y hacemos un llamamiento a la unidad en torno a los valores del deporte. La crispación y el sabotaje no resuelven ningún problema. Ni el Rayo, ni el Athletic se merecían esta situación. Respeto”. El último en pronunciarse fue el club, que emitió un extenso comunicado condenando los hechos. En el inicio del escrito se carga contra "un grupo organizado", que ha tenido la finalidad "de detener el encuentro hasta provocar su suspensión". "Se ha atentado contra la seguridad de los jugadores, los árbitros presentes en el terreno de juego, contra la libertad de estos para ejercer su profesión y de la mayoría de los aficionados desplazados al estadio esta tarde", refiriéndose al lanzamiento de aviones de papel y pelotas de pequeñas dimensiones. En el resto del comunicado se cita a "Bukaneros", "Plataforma ADRV" y a la "Federación de Peñas" como instigadores de la creación de estos hechos. "Han emitido comunicados que hacían prever una situación de gran hostilidad como la que se ha producido". A la salida de más protagonistas, Beñat San José confirmó la intención de que el equipo realizara el día de hoy su sesión de entrenamiento, mientras que el Athletic Club confirmó su vuelta a Bilbao en la misma tarde del sábado. La única vía para que el encuentro pueda celebrarse es que el Rayo - Athletic se celebre a puerta cerrada en la fecha que considere el Comité de Competición.

Y ambos, además, lo hicieron a lo grande. Los ilicitanos ganaron a domicilio al Espanyol en un encuentro en el que jugaron con uno menos desde el minuto 6 y los celestes golearon en Balaídos al Racing de Santander, al que le endosaron una manita. Retoma LaLiga con la moral alta y con ganas de dar la primera alegría a la afición en el Martínez Valero, donde ha firmado su peor inicio en Primera con tres derrotas seguidas. En las dos últimas, ante Real Sociedad (2-3) y Real Madrid (2-3), igualó un 0-2 y cayó con un gol en los últimos compases. Martín Anselmi deberá modificar la zaga por la baja de Fede Redondo, expulsado en el RCDE Stadium. Bigas apunta a ocupar su sitio. El resto del once será similar. Sangaré, que salió lesionado en el último compromiso, se recuperó en el parón. Josan también estará disponible, después de quedar en libertad sin cargos tras ser detenido por presuntos malos tratos el pasado martes. Intenta reiniciar la competición, tal y como la finalizó antes del parón. No conoce la derrota en LaLiga como visitante. Insiste el técnico en que la prioridad pasa por este partido, aparcando hasta después la esperada cita de Europa League del jueves en Balaídos ante la Juventus. Aspas, ya con el alta, vuelve a la convocatoria, en la que no figuran por lesión Miguel Román, Starfelt y Jones El-Abdellaoui. Bajas sensibles, fundamentalmente la del mediocampista por su importancia en el esquema de Giráldez. Fer Niño vs Durán. Los dos, que están en plena forma, vienen de marcar un doblete en la pasada jornada. El del Elche, además, acumula otros tres tantos en el campeonato y ya lleva cinco. Al Elche le está costando en casa y el Celta no ha perdido a domicilio. Los celestes, además, dieron el estirón que necesitaban convirtiendo su juego en goles la pasada jornada. Son un equipo peligroso.

articles.summary: Los verdiblancos buscan prolongar su racha como locales ante un equipo en dificultades
articles.body: Después de una larguísima fecha FIFA de selecciones, Betis y Osasuna retoman esta tarde la competición viéndose las caras en el Estadio La Cartuja (18.30 horas por Movistar LaLiga TV), en el partido correspondiente a la octava jornada del torneo doméstico. Los verdiblancos, tras su prometedor arranque de curso y después de 14 partidos de Liga seguidos en su estadio sin perder, reciben a un conjunto rojillo herido, que no gana desde agosto y acumula tres derrotas en sus cuatro últimos compromisos... pero que busca en reaccionar en Sevilla. El equipo de Pellegrini afronta su regreso a la competición desde dos puntos de vista diferentes. Por un lado, tener que parar cuando marchaba en una dinámica muy positiva siempre genera ciertas dudas sobre si será capaz de mantener la velocidad de crucero en la que marchaba. Por otro, este largo parón le ha servido para recuperar a Bartra y Diego Llorente y para que jugadores llamados a ser importantes como Ceballos o Lo Celso avancen en su puesta a punto con una 'mini pretemporada' después de un verano sin trabajo con el grupo. A excepción de Fran García, todo apunta a que los jugadores que se quedaron en casa durante el parón tendrán un mayor protagonismo de inicio, con la duda entre Deossa y Riquelme, principalmente. El conjunto rojillo llega a La Cartuja, uno de los escenarios más complicados de la categoría, con la necesidad imperiosa de mostrar un buen nivel de juego y, sobre todo, de retomar la senda de los buenos resultados. Osasuna no gana desde finales de agosto y sólo ha sumado uno de los 12 últimos puntos en juego. Las bajas de última hora de Aimar Oroz y Kike Barja pueden hacer más mella si cabe en los planes de Luis Miguel Ramis. Aunque la buena noticia llega de la mano de Moi Gómez y Rosier, a los que recupera para la causa. Cucho vs Budimir: Buena parte de las opciones de victoria de Betis y Osasuna esta tarde pasarán por las botas de sus delanteros. En los verdiblancos, el colombiano apunta al once ante un rival al que ha marcado en dos de sus tres últimos enfrentamientos. Con dos tantos y una asistencia en lo que va de campeonato, Cucho sabe que este año debe dar su mejor versión por la fuerte competencia con Parrott. En el lado rojillo, el croata suma cinco de las seis dianas de su equipo en LaLiga en lo que va de temporada. Al Betis le ha hecho seis en 12 enfrentamientos, aunque viene de jugar con su selección y con menos descanso... * Datos de Opta, Bdfutbol y Documentación MARCA

José Alberto y la plantilla han reconocido que las tres semanas sin jugar les ha venido bien para limpiar la cabeza después de los batacazos ante Barcelona y Celta. Para este choque el técnico racingiuista recupera prácticamente a toda la plantilla a excepción de Eriksson. Las dudas en el once se centran de medio campo hacía delante. Andrés ya recuperado puede ser la sorpresa en el once de inicio.

articles.title: Una trituradora sin pausa
articles.standfirst: El Barcelona mantiene su altísimo nivel competitivo
articles.summary: El Barcelona mantiene su altísimo nivel competitivo
articles.body: El Barcelona había comenzado la temporada de manera demoledora. Contaba sus partidos por victorias. Y no solo eso: el juego que estaba ofreciendo el equipo de Flick era excelente, con una media goleadora asombrosa. En los ocho partidos oficiales que había disputado, promediaba 4,5 tantos por encuentro. Una barbaridad, teniendo en cuenta que el equipo había renovado en verano la mitad de su delantera. El parón de selecciones no fue una buena noticia. En primer lugar, porque, sin ninguna duda, interrumpía el excelente ritmo que llevaban los azulgranas. Y, por otra parte, porque esos parones siempre le han pasado factura al Barcelona en forma de lesiones. El historial es extenso. En esta ocasión, aunque no ha sido nada grave, le tocó el turno a Raphinha, que había sido el mejor de los azulgranas en esos primeros partidos. Sin embargo, a la hora de la verdad, el parón fue simplemente eso, un paréntesis, porque el Barcelona sigue a lo suyo: ganando partidos y, además, haciéndolo con holgura en el marcador. Asimismo, a la vista de lo que se avecina en el calendario, Flick echó mano de las rotaciones. Dejó en el banquillo de entrada a jugadores como Cubarsí, Pedri o Fermín, además del mencionado Raphinha. Pero el Barcelona ya funciona a velocidad de crucero, juegue quien juegue. No fue el mejor partido del Barcelona, pero este equipo está a un nivel que no necesita brillar para imponerse con facilidad a cualquier rival. Esta vez le tocó al Getafe, un equipo que sabe defender muy bien y que podía poner las cosas muy complicadas. Gordon, que anotó en el primer minuto de juego, y Gabriel Jesús tomaron el relevo de Raphinha, y la tarde fue plácida para los azulgranas. Una excelente noticia para el Barcelona ahora que el calendario empieza a complicarse. El equipo de Flick tendrá que demostrar que es capaz de rendir al mismo nivel cuando lleguen compromisos de mayor exigencia. De entrada, los próximos tres partidos serán lejos del Camp Nou y no resultarán fáciles, si bien es cierto que el Barcelona está ofreciendo el mismo rendimiento tanto dentro como fuera de casa. El primer envite será en el campo del Galatasaray. Nunca es fácil ganar en Turquía, pero, a priori, no es el partido más complicado que tienen los azulgranas en las próximas fechas. Después jugarán en el campo del Betis, que está ofreciendo un gran rendimiento en este inicio de temporada. En su estadio, sin ir más lejos, cayó el Real Madrid. A partir de ahí sí llegarán los compromisos realmente complicados. En primer lugar, los azulgranas viajarán a París para enfrentarse al PSG en el Parque de los Príncipes. Medirse al actual campeón de Europa supone un auténtico reto. Después llegará el gran choque del año: el primer Clásico de la temporada, que se celebrará en el Camp Nou. A la vista de su rendimiento actual, los de Flick no tienen por qué temer a ningún rival.

articles.title: El Atlético a domicilio, una maldición con caducidad
articles.standfirst: Tras el triunfo en Mendizorroza que se une al del Pizjuán y al de Anoeta, los de Simeone vuelven a ser fiables lejos del Metropolitano: nueve puntos de 12
articles.summary: Tras el triunfo en Mendizorroza que se une al del Pizjuán y al de Anoeta, los de Simeone vuelven a ser fiables lejos del Metropolitano: nueve puntos de 12
articles.body: Ha sido la maldición del Atlético durante las últimas temporadas. Lo que se ganaba en el Metropolitano, se perdía cuando se viajaba. Y así hasta dejar escapar Liga tras Liga. Una cruz que había que quitarse, sin duda, como uno de los grandes objetivos del campeonato. Cuando van ocho jornadas, cuatro de ellas fuera, los de Simeone han logrado esa fiabilidad a domicilio vital para poder aspirar al campeonato al menos hasta los últimos meses. De hecho, el balance es de 9 de los 12 puntos ganados, siendo el traspiés de San Mamés el único del conjunto del Metropolitano. Un partido que pese al 3-0 final no fue tan malo como dice el resultado. El resto de salidas, por ahí, han sido más que positivas. Se ganó en el Sánchez Pijuán y se repitió en Anoeta. Un balance de 1-6 en dos de los campos que más dolores de cabeza dan a los rojiblancos y a la mayoría de equipos de LaLiga. Con la victoria de ayer en Mendizorroza, un conjunto que está siendo una de las grandes revelaciones del campeonato, los del Cholo parecen despejar la maldición a domicilio. Las siguientes salidas (estadios del Espanyol y el Levante) parecen propicias para seguir sumando de tres en tres, algo que viene haciendo el Atlético en los últimos tiempos como demuestra los cuatro triunfos seguidos (se goleó a Osasuna y se venció al Madrid en el derbi). Más allá de que el Atlético mantiene el segundo puesto con la victoria, el problema está siendo el impecable ritmo del Barça. Con el triunfo ante el Getafe son 24 puntos de 24 y una sensación de que los de Flick se dejarán pocos puntos en este campeonato. Los de Simeone, mientras, son al menos los que les aguantan el pulso.

articles.title: Kentucky's 2-point call pays off in 35-34 overtime win over No. 10 LSU
articles.summary: The Wildcats have now won overtime games by the same score in back-to-back weeks.
articles.body:
Kentucky got its second consecutive overtime win by the same 35-34 score on Saturday night.

A week after beating South Carolina on the road, the Wildcats upset No. 10 LSU on QB Kenny Minchey's 2-point conversion run. The Wildcats are the first team in FBS history — remember, overtime was implemented in 1996 — to win back-to-back games by a single point in OT.

The decision to go for the game-winning conversion came after some gamesmanship between both LSU coach Lane Kiffin and Kentucky coach Will Stein. After Kiffin called timeout when Kentucky lined up to go for the win, Stein returned the favor on the next formation just barely before one of his players committed a false start penalty.

If the play wasn't a quarterback draw, it might as well have been. Minchey dropped back to pass and there were no defenders in the middle of the field as he waltzed into the end zone for the win.

The victory also comes a week after Kentucky inexplicably fell out of the AP Top 25 after the South Carolina win. The Wildcats (5-1) were No. 24 entering the game in South Carolina and came back from an early 17-0 deficit. They somehow dropped out of the poll entirely after the victory and entered Saturday's game against the Tigers unranked.

Not only will Kentucky (5-1) be ranked on Sunday, the Wildcats don't have any games remaining against teams who entered Week 6 in the top 10. Kentucky may hang around in the thick of the SEC title game race for a while.

LSU, meanwhile, is on the College Football Playoff precipice already. With games remaining against Mississippi State, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee, the Tigers (4-2) may not be able to afford another loss and still make the 12-team field.

A big reason for that? QB Sam Leavitt's turnovers. Leavitt had an interception and a fumble in the second half against the Wildcats, and LSU is incredibly fortunate that Kentucky didn't win in regulation. UK kicker Adam Zouagui missed a go-ahead 26-yard field goal with 3:11 to go when Leavitt fumbled at the LSU 13. That was Zouagui's second miss of the quarter, and Kentucky turned the ball over on downs in the third quarter after Leavitt's pick.

Leavitt has now thrown eight interceptions across six games in 2026. Over 20 games at Arizona State in 2024 and 2025, he threw nine interceptions across 589 pass attempts.

articles.title: Georgia Beats Alabama, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Keelon Russell, Gunner Stockton
articles.summary: Both the Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide entered Saturday undefeated, but only one left with its perfect record intact.
articles.body:
Both the Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide entered Saturday undefeated, but only one left with its perfect record intact.

Georgia overcame a handful of near-costly mistakes to escape with a 20-17 road victory over Alabama on Saturday.

Alabama entered Bryant-Denny Stadium as a 2.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but suffered its first loss of the season after failing to find the end zone in the second half.

Despite an opening-drive fumble that set up a Georgia field goal, Alabama rallied from an early 3-0 deficit to take a 14-10 lead into halftime, scoring two late touchdowns to seize momentum.

Russell connected with tight end Marshall Pritchett for a 22-yard touchdown before the Crimson Tide capped a quick 1:42 drive with an EJ Crowell rushing score.

Georgia found the endzone in the second quarter on a 20-yard touchdown pass from Stockton to London Humphreys. On the following possession, Stockton threw just his second interception of the season, but Alabama failed to turn the takeaway into points.

Georgia struck coming out of halftime, with Stockton capping a 75-yard drive with a 14-yard rushing touchdown to give the Bulldogs a 17-14 lead.

Alabama tied the game with a field goal in the third quarter, while its defense came close to forcing multiple turnovers in the second half. Georgia continued to dodge trouble, escaping several close calls to maintain its lead.

Georgia's Peyton Woodring missed a field goal from 39-yards out, but nailed one from 23-yards to give the Bull Dogs a 20-17 lead with 5:25 remaining.

A costly personal foul by Alabama proved decisive, allowing Georgia to run out the clock and seal the victory.

Alabama will travel to Tennessee to face the No. 15 Volunteers next Saturday, while Georgia hosts the Auburn Tigers. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: "Terzic no se lo podía creer"
articles.standfirst: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.summary: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.body: Esto no es Anfield, pero es divertido. LaLiga, antes la Liga, retornó a lo grande como El Cordobés cuando volvía a los ruedos. El semipartido de Vallecas fue un salto de la rana, un suceso estrafalario que cotizaba en las casas de apuestas. Se había anunciado jarana en el minuto 13, un minuto anti-Ángel Nieto, cuyo nombre es como el código postal de la barriada. En ese instante, sin derrapar, se desató un Pearl Harbor de papel y bolas. El partido, dirigido por Sánchez Martínez, alias Manolete con perdón (dale con los toros), no levantó cabeza. El colegiado dio una lección de protocolo. Puede organizar una comida real o un aterrizaje y salir a hombros. Los avioncitos lanzados al césped viajaban con libro de instrucciones como una lavadora o un recién nacido. Una parte de la afición de Vallecas no quiere ser nominada para el Óscar a la Paciencia, premio para el que debería luchar con otros colectivos situados en Valencia o Zaragoza, por poner al azar algún ejemplo. Las imágenes ahorraban planos de la hierba, la grada, los objetos y el palco, algo así como si vas a informar de una acampada y enfocas al cielo. En un descuido se grabó a Raúl Martín Presa, algo menos popular que Messi en Rosario y en Benin. En la masa de hormigas en el césped había que fijarse en Edin Terzic, que tenía cara de alemán que a esa hora estaría mejor en una tumbona en Cádiz. El técnico del Athletic vivió un día para contarlo. Él viene de Dortmund, el hogar del llamado 'muro amarillo', una grada legendaria en el mundo. En Vallecas se encontró con otro muro, el de cemento detrás de una portería. Allí había entradas baratas. Hay que imaginar la sorpresa sideral de Terzic cuando atisbó el estado de las instalaciones de un estadio de Primera. En verano, Martín Presa achacó en serio la suciedad de la bombonera vallecana durante años a la superpoblación de palomas. Esta explicación ya es historia del fútbol. Luego Terzic acudió al congreso de especialistas montado por el árbitro en la hierba para comunicarles la suspensión del encuentro. Parecía necesitar intérprete para entender lo que se contaba. A falta de Berlanga si se pasan por allí los Javis les sale un documental precioso. El desalojo, puestos a buscar algo positivo, fue pacífico y cantarín. Del ‘Presa, vete ya’ se pasó a lo de ‘a la vida pirata se vive mejor’. El Rayo de las cañas, las bravas y la franja es una lista de Spotify. Que no pare la música. Terzic, esto es lo que hay.

articles.title: Messi prolonga su fiesta
articles.standfirst: Inter Miami tumba 4-0 al DC United con dobletes de Leo y Luis Suárez
articles.summary: Inter Miami tumba 4-0 al DC United con dobletes de Leo y Luis Suárez
articles.body: Solo cuatro días después de su emotiva despedida de la selección argentina, Lionel Messi dio otro festival de fútbol con el Inter Miami al anotar un doblete, al igual que Luis Suárez, en el contundente 4-0 endosado al DC United en el NU Stadium. Messi alcanzó los 23 goles en lo que va de la MLS y es cada vez más el máximo artillero de la liga. Suárez también fue protagonista al anotar los dos goles que pusieron cuesta abajo el duelo en la primera mitad. Después de su multitudinaria despedida de la selección argentina, el pasado 6 de octubre en Buenos Aires en el amistoso contra Benín, Messi salió de titular en En esta fecha FIFA extendida a tres semanas, Messi logró disputar todos los partidos del Inter Miami y se desplazó a Argentina solo para el histórico encuentro del pasado martes, en el que anotó un gol y dio dos asistencias. el once de Cristian González para enfrentarse al DC United. Si también se considera el compromiso internacional, Messi lleva cinco partidos consecutivos marcando. Anotó el primero nada más comenzar la segunda mitad al rematar dentro del área una asistencia de Suárez. Fue a la hora de partido cuando Messi culminó su gran noche con una maravilla. Logró un eslalon espectacular entre tres defensas para entrar en el área y fulminar al portero con un remate cruzado que desató la euforia del público del NU Stadium. Intercambió un abrazo con sus compañeros, incluido un Luis Suárez que anotó sus dos goles en la primera mitad al aprovechar dos asistencias de Germán Berterame. El Inter Miami es segundo en el Este con 49 puntos, detrás de un Nashville que arrancó la jornada con 60 puntos.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: After a tumultuous day of upsets, Georgia left no doubt about who's No. 1 with win over Alabama
articles.summary: UCLA knocked off Oregon on the road, UK outlasted LSU in an OT thriller and Oklahoma toppled Texas in a chaotic Red River finish. Week 6 delivered in a big w...
articles.body:
If a first-year UCLA coach winning in Eugene wasn't enough for you, if Mike Elko ridiculing his own fan base didn't do it for you, if Kentucky knocking off LSU in overtime didn't stun you enough, the No. 1 team in the land decided to cough up a game in Dallas.

In our Top 10 rankings, the Texas Longhorns took a tumble after a stumble against the Oklahoma Sooners in the Red River Rivalry at the Cotton Bowl.

Arch Manning's two interceptions and a last-second OU field goal shuffled our rankings after a wild Week 6 of college football.

The Bruins, under first-year coach Bob Chesney, surged into our poll after beating Oregon and moving to 5-0. Welcome to Missouri as well, which drubbed Texas A&M so much that Elko bashed his fan base . And Kentucky converted a 2-point conversion for a second straight week to win in overtime, downing LSU to move to 5-1 under first-year coach Will Stein.

Meanwhile, Indiana remains in the Top 10 by storming back to win in Lincoln and the Vols survived a scare in Fayetteville to set up a big game against Alabama in Knoxville on Saturday. Speaking of Alabama, the Tide lost a prize fight at home to Georgia .

You won't find the Florida Gators in the poll either after a second consecutive beating — this one at home to reeling South Carolina. In the ACC, Bill Belichick got his first ranked win in Chapel Hill with a win at previously undefeated Pitt, and Duke dropped out of the unbeatens with a loss in Atlanta.

In Big 12 land, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Houston all got big wins to put themselves in position to challenge Texas Tech, BYU and Utah for the league crown. And in the nightcap, USC won a game in the Eastern Time Zone (gasp!) at Penn State to keep its playoff hopes alive.

Kirby Smart got his first regular season win over Alabama in a decade in Tuscaloosa. It's tough to believe, but the former Tide assistant was 0-7 in regular season matchups (he did win a national title and SEC championship game against Bama). QB Gunner Stockton threw for 248 yards and the Bulldogs ran right over the Tide for 206 yards on the ground in a dominant showing on the line of scrimmage.

During ESPN's popular pregame show, "College GameDay," analysts Kirk Herbstreit and Nick Saban answered an important question: Who has the best team in college football right now? Their answer, they both agreed, was none other than the Hurricanes. After a week off, Miami hosts reeling Florida State. Aside from Notre Dame in South Bend on Nov. 7, UM might not play another ranked opponent in the regular season. That light schedule doesn't mean the Canes aren't real. QB Darian Mensah has almost more touchdowns (15) than incompletions (19)!

The Terrapins didn't stand a chance against the Buckeyes. Maryland had one drive of more than 22 yards and needed an interception return for a touchdown just to eclipse the 10-point mark. WR Jeremiah Smith had a down game. He only had 93 yards on four catches and, oh yeah, caught two touchdown passes as well. QB Julian Sayin finished a game with at least three touchdowns for a third straight week.

This was a tough one. In the second half, the Crimson Tide had an interception overturned on video review (did it hit the ground?) and they didn't get the benefit of a pass interference penalty in the end zone on a late game drive (let's be honest, it was pass interference). Alabama isn't out of the playoff race, though. Far from it, in fact. But next week's game in Knoxville now looms as a near postseason elimination game.

RB Jonaz Walton scored on 40- and 97-yard runs and Notre Dame's defense held the Cardinal to just 202 yards of offense and stopped them on nine of 11 third-down attempts. It's time to look forward to next week. The Irish face their first ranked opponent of the season with a game at BYU. The Cougars will be hosting ESPN's "College GameDay." Buckle up for a weeklong buildup. Is Notre Dame real? We'll find out soon enough.

Get ready for more talk about the woes of Texas' offense and QB Arch Manning. He threw two costly second-half interceptions. OU's game-winning field goal came after Manning's last pick with 19 seconds left. Despite a 150-yard advantage in total yards, the Horns stumbled to a stinging loss to their archrival and they plummeted in our rankings. But don't forget that Steve Sarkisian's program still gets points for the win over Ohio State.

Thank goodness the Hoosiers have Nick Marsh. The former Michigan State receiver scored on 75- and 44-yard passes from Josh Hoover in the final quarter to overcome an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. Marsh's game-winning reception came on a nifty play design that originated from Kansas coach Lance Leipold, according to Indiana coach Curt Cignetti. The score helped Indiana extend its nation-leading winning streak of 22 games — the second-longest for any Big Ten team. The longest belongs to Ohio State at 23 (2013-14). The Hoosiers host the Buckeyes next week.

First-year coach Bob Chesney and the Bruins are 5-0 after the victory in Eugene. UCLA's defense forced seven — seven! — Oregon turnovers. What was most surprising of all is that Chesney's team did it with backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who replaced injured starter Nico Iamaleava in the second half. The Bruins return to LA for three straight home games against Wisconsin, Michigan State and Nevada. An 8-0 record is not out of the question!

This trip to Fayetteville wasn't so pretty. The Hogs, in fact, led 14-10 in the third quarter and tied the game with about 7 minutes left. Replacing benched starter Faizon Brandon, George MacIntyre threw for 247 yards but it was the Tennessee ground game that won it at the very end. DeSean Bishop ripped off a 59-yard run on UT's first play of what was a five-play, 94-yard, game-winning touchdown drive.

After a loss at Mississippi State, Eli Drinkwitz's team has won two straight at home in bludgeon fashion, outscoring A&M and Florida 72-23 in back-to-back weeks. Drinkwitz is doing wonders with former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons, who had some key runs on Saturday, and RB Jamal Roberts had another big day. He's eclipsed 200 yards in consecutive weeks as he continues to replace Ahmad Hardy, who is still recovering from a gunshot wound.

articles.title: Everything Lane Kiffin Said After LSU's Stunning OT Loss vs. Kentucky Drops Record to 4-2
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin and LSU came into the season as presumed College Football Playoff contenders, but they're now 4-2 after an upset loss to Kentucky in overtime.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin and LSU came into the season as presumed College Football Playoff contenders, but they're now 4-2 after an upset loss to Kentucky in overtime.

Kiffin's immediate reaction to the loss was his team's lack of execution. He specifically noted a punt that the Wildcats returned for a touchdown to take the lead in the second quarter.

"If you don't execute, you don't execute," Kiffin told reporters. "The punt return, you got a player there tackling him and doesn't tackle him, and he goes outside and, you know, on the long run, he swooped out of a gap and the ball goes for a long run. If you don't do fundamentally sound stuff, you get exposed versus good teams."

The Tigers' lack of execution was mostly on the defensive side. Kentucky's CJ Baxter rushed for 123 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Quarterback Kenny Minchey threw for 246 yards and practically walked into the end zone on the Wildcats' two-point conversion in overtime.

Kentucky gave LSU plenty of chances to win late. The Wildcats missed what would have been a game-tying field goal in the final minutes, but the Tigers couldn't get the first down needed to ice the game.

"When the chance comes in the fourth quarter, you can't let 'em hang around," Kiffin told reporters . "We had the ball ahead and then we turned the ball over. And another chance to end it there so they don't get it back. Obviously, things go the other way, you look at yourself first."

That allowed Kentucky to march down the field and get another chance to tie it, and they took advantage of it and sent the game to overtime.

LSU was mostly sound on offense. Sam Leavitt threw for 275 yards and two touchdowns, though he threw an interception and fumbled the ball once.

The Tigers' season is still salvageable, but the loss makes their path to the CFP much harder. LSU still has to face Mississippi State, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee, all ranked teams, and it will likely need to win out to be one of the last 12 teams standing.

"This goes on all of us," Kiffin said. "We had all kinds of chances to close the game out and win the game, and didn't do it. You let people hang around on the road at night in the SEC, that's gonna happen."

articles.title: Who's the Favorite? Beautiful Chaos Ruling College Football at Midpoint of 2026 Season
articles.summary: We still don't know.
articles.body:
Six weeks into the 2026 college football season, our opinions are starting to build a backbone. You believe in that school. I'm all-in on this program. The struggling teams? They're just pretenders.

The beauty of this all, though, is any number of teams could be plugged into the undefined places of those sentences.

Georgia, for example, picked up a massive win Saturday at Alabama. While the Dawgs deserve the praise for the victory—they've stood atop B/R's Top 25 for several weeks, too—it took every bit of 60 minutes for UGA to clip the Crimson Tide.

At the midpoint of the campaign, there's no undisputed top team.

Georgia has a strong case, absolutely. Still, it's fair to mention the toughest part of UGA's schedule is only now arriving. Rivalry games against Auburn and Florida are up next, followed by a trip to Ole Miss and clash with Missouri. Taking down Alabama on the road is fantastic, but plenty more tests are ahead.

You could tout Notre Dame or Miami, a pair of Top Five programs. Both appear destined for a spot in the CFP, no matter what happens in the Nov. 7 clash featuring the now-undefeated teams.

Between them, though, what's their best win? Wisconsin? Wake Forest?

Scan the rest of the nation's unbeatens, and you're not going to find an incredibly dominant, runaway-type of team.

Indiana held off Northwestern and needed a comeback to survive Nebraska on Saturday. BYU hasn't scored more than 28 points in three Big 12 matchups. Texas Tech and Utah have played a low level of competition on the path to 5-0, similar to—yes, it's true—UCLA. James Madison rounds out the group.

Texas became the most prominent loser in Week 6, imploding during the fourth quarter of a frustrating setback to rival Oklahoma. Saturday's slate also ended the perfect records of Duke, Pitt and North Dakota State, along with Nebraska and Alabama in their marquee games.

Beyond that, preseason hopefuls LSU and Oregon endured their second losses of the campaign. Florida fell for the second week in a row.

Ohio State and Ole Miss already had a loss apiece, as did Tennessee and USC. The mood around teams like Michigan, Oklahoma and Texas A&M has soured—and an upset of Texas isn't enough evidence needed to suddenly buy OU, given the Sooners' early mess on offense.

Pick any team not mentioned, and we could easily find a bad result, an obvious flaw or an uphill climb.

We still don't know. That's the best part.

The second half of the 2026 season doesn't have a seemingly inevitable ending. Georgia heads to Ole Miss in a month for a critical SEC tilt. In addition to the later showdown with Miami, Notre Dame is set to play BYU—which also travels to Utah—in Week 7 as Indiana hosts Ohio State.

UCLA's schedule is incredibly favorable, and Iowa lands in that category, too. But are we genuinely ready to trust the Bruins or Hawkeyes?

Ole Miss, conversely, is hugely talented with a nightmare slate remaining, and Texas' path is comparably brutal. Kentucky, Missouri and Mississippi State have impressed early but will be challenged often in the SEC.

Houston and Oklahoma State are bracing for a prime-time meeting in Week 7, and a future date with a Big 12 unbeaten awaits both. Ohio State has a difficult three-game run surging over the horizon, as well.

So often in college football, there's an overwhelming team or two just cruising toward the postseason by the halfway point of the campaign. And, hey, in hindsight, we might say UGA, Notre Dame or Miami fit that billing.

But as mid-October closes in, the strongest opinions you or I might hold about the championship favorite—well, they are either unproven or a confident guess.

We still don't know. And I, for one, can hardly wait to find out.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 6
articles.summary: Chaos in the SEC was the headline in Week 6 of the 2026 college football season, while the marquee matchup of Alabama and Georgia lived up to the hype in a tight game that was decided by a late field goal.
articles.body:
Chaos in the SEC was the headline in Week 6 of the 2026 college football season, while the marquee matchup of Alabama and Georgia lived up to the hype in a tight game that was decided by a late field goal.

When the dust settled on Saturday's action, Texas, LSU and Florida had all suffered upset losses to shake up the SEC picture, while ACC contenders Pittsburgh and Duke both took their first losses of the season to open up multiple spots at the bottom of the rankings.

All of that led to plenty of shuffling in our weekly rankings, and ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 6 action.

25. Boise State (4-1, Previous Rank: 25)

Week 6 Result: Winning at Fresno State (25-20, halftime) Next Week: BYE

Full analysis will be added after the game is over.

24. James Madison (6-0, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 6 Result: WIN at Georgia Southern (27-24) Next Week: vs. Georgia State

After a 12-2 finish a year ago that earned them a trip to the College Football Playoff, the Dukes are once again one of the nation's best Group of Six teams. Despite surrendering 465 yards of offense on the night, they were able to weather a pair of fourth-quarter touchdown drives from Georgia Southern to hang on for a three-point victory. The defense dug in and forced a 52-yard field goal attempt from the Eagles with 47 seconds remaining that was missed to clinch the win.

Week 6 Result: LOSS vs. Indiana (17-20) Next Week: at Oregon

The Cornhuskers almost pulled off the upset, with a 17-6 lead early in the fourth quarter following a 39-yard rushing touchdown from quarterback Anthony Colandrea. However, the defense allowed back-to-back touchdown drives on the other side of that score, and the offense finished the game with a punt and two turnovers on downs. It's the first loss of the year for Nebraska, but a solid performance against a title-level contender. Next week's matchup against Oregon will draw the line between contender and pretend for the Cornhuskers.

Week 6 Result: WIN at West Virginia (52-31) Next Week: BYE

After a 34-7 victory over a previously undefeated Cincinnati team a week ago, Arizona hung a season-high 52 points on West Virginia, and they are averaging 40.5 points over their last four games since losing to BYU. Noah Fifita (16/23, 341 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT) had another big day through the air, while the Wildcats defense did a good job bottling up Mountaineers quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. (25 carries, 98 yards, 1 TD), who entered the game with 574 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns through five games.

21. Wake Forest (5-1, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 6 Result: WIN at NC State (38-14) Next Week: at California

Gio Lopez torched the NC State secondary for 303 yards and three touchdowns while completing 26 of 33 pass attempts. He had two passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown during the third quarter, and those 21 unanswered points helped put the game away after the Wolfpack kept things close during the first half. On the defensive side of the ball, NC State was limited to 15 rushing yards on 25 attempts and 258 total yards of offense.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Arkansas (24-17) Next Week: vs. Alabama

George MacIntyre had 247 yards and a touchdown, but he also threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in his first start. He started in place of struggling freshman Faizon Brandon, who has underperformed and is also dealing with a shoulder injury. DeSean Bishop (19 carries, 138 yards, 1 TD) picked up the slack offensively, while the defense forced eight punts and kept the Arkansas offense from building any momentum aside from a pair of third quarter touchdown drives.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Kansas State (35-16) Next Week: vs. Oklahoma State

Conner Weigman threw for 242 yards and four touchdowns, and tight end Patrick Overmyer was on the receiving end of all four of those scores. The running game nearly matched that production with 43 carries for 233 yards in a well-balanced offensive game by the Cougars. An eight-play, 76-yard drive early in the third quarter that ended in Overmyer's third touchdown catch gave Houston a commanding 28-3 lead, so the game was not even as close as the final score suggests.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Washington (41-24) Next Week: BYE

With starting quarterback Hank Brown sidelined with a shoulder injury, the Hawkeyes still hung 41 points on the Washington defense. Backup Jeremy Hecklinski (14/19, 202 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) was effective when asked to throw, while Kamari Moulton (26 carries, 208 yards, 2 TD) opened up the passing game with his stellar work on the ground. A solid overall response from Iowa following their Week 5 loss to Ohio State.

17. Oklahoma State (4-1, Previous Rank: 21)

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. UCF (42-28) Next Week: at Houston

The Cowboys managed to pull away late in a game where they trailed 14-7 at the end of the first quarter and were tied 21-21 at halftime. Drew Mestemaker (19/28, 304 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) had his fourth straight 300-yard passing game, and Oklahoma State has won all of them after a season-opening upset loss to Tulsa. The offense is averaging 45.3 points in their four victories, and next week's matchup with Houston could be a shootout.

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. LSU (35-34, OT) Next Week: at Oklahoma

For the second week in a row, Kentucky won by one point on a two-point conversion in overtime, as head coach Will Stein has played for the win and his team has delivered. CJ Baxter was the standout offensively, tallying 19 carries for 123 yards and two touchdowns, and he scored the touchdown in overtime. Then it was quarterback Kenny Minchey on a keeper for the game-winning conversion, giving the Wildcats a huge win over the No. 10 team in the latest AP poll.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Penn State (31-23) Next Week: BYE

Jayden Maiava (21/33, 301 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT), King Miller (19 carries, 102 yards, 1 TD) and Trent Mosley (9 catches, 111 yards, 1 TD) all had standout games for the Trojans. The difference in the game was the start of the second half, as USC responded to a pair of Penn State drives that ended in field goals by capping off their own drives with touchdowns. A forced fumble with under four minutes to play iced the victory for the Trojans, and that was the only turnover of the game on either side.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Oregon (17-15) Next Week: vs. Wisconsin

The UCLA defense had five fumble recoveries and two interceptions, helping to offset three turnovers from their own offense in an ugly game. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava missed the second half with a leg injury after throwing two interceptions in the first half, leaving Wayne Knight (22 carries, 103 yards, 1 TD) to shoulder the load offensively in their run-heavy attack. It wasn't pretty, but a 5-0 start and a win over a ranked opponent is a successful weekend.

13. Mississippi State (4-1, Previous Rank: 17)

The Bulldogs' upstart story ran into a brick wall last week when they suffered a 56-23 loss at home against Alabama, but this still looks like a team capable of hanging around in the national picture. Quarterback Kamario Taylor entered Week 6 leading the SEC in passing yards (1,450) and passing touchdowns (17), and he has been one of college football's biggest breakout stars. A road game against LSU coming out of their bye week presents a golden opportunity to get their CFP hopes back on track.

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. Texas A&M (27-6) Next Week: at Ole Miss

The Aggies simply had no answer for the Missouri defense, as the Tigers allowed 196 total yards and only nine first downs while surrendering just a pair of field goals. That was backed by a busy day for running back Jamal Roberts, who had a season-high 34 carries for 222 yards and two touchdowns, with Missouri finishing with a staggering 254-29 edge in rushing yardage. Another good win for a team whose only blemish is a seven-point loss on the road to a good Mississippi State squad.

Week 6 Result: WIN at Vanderbilt (52-17) Next Week: vs. Missouri

The Rebels had a bye week to recover from their upset loss to Florida, and they came out the other side with a dominant showing on the road. The defense had four takeaways, eight tackles for loss, three sacks and a touchdown, holding the Commodores to just three points in the first half. On offense, Trinidad Chambliss had 213 passing yards and four total touchdowns, while the running game was good for 196 yards and three scores.

Week 6 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Arizona State

The Red Raiders are 5-0 for the second year in a row, though this group has been less dominant than the team that finished 12-2 a year ago and made the College Football Playoff. Quarterback Will Hammond has been inconsistent with five touchdowns and five interceptions, but the defense has racked up 10 takeaways and the running game has averaged 179.0 yards per game with 12 touchdowns.

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. Kansas (41-24) Next Week: at Colorado

Quarterback Devon Dampier had a standout game with his arm and his legs, finishing with 238 passing yards, 71 rushing yards and four total touchdowns to help the Utes improve to 2-0 in Big 12 play and stay undefeated on the year. It was 21-17 at halftime and 27-24 through three quarters, but the Utes pulled away with a pair of touchdown drives in the fourth quarter and a pair of turnovers on downs forced by the defense.

Week 6 Result: LOSS at Oklahoma (24-27) Next Week: vs. Florida

After tight-roping to victory against Ohio State (24-23) and Tennessee (20-17) earlier this season, the Longhorns were on the wrong end of a late comeback on Saturday. With a pick-six, a missed field goal and another interception thrown by Arch Manning all in the fourth quarter, Texas simply gave away too many opportunities down the stretch. The Sooners were outgained significantly in total yardage, but took a 24-17 lead with consecutive touchdowns in the fourth quarter. The Longhorns tied it up with a 75-yard touchdown drive of their own, but Tate Sandell drilled the game-winning, 47-yard field goal as time expired.

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. Iowa State (24-10) Next Week: vs. Notre Dame

In a game that was more lopsided than the final score suggests, BYU outgained Iowa State by a 506-200 margin in total yardage. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier had 329 passing yards, 109 rushing yards and two touchdowns, and the Cougars defense limited the Cyclones to 2-of-13 on third-down conversions while forcing seven punts and one turnover on downs. Next week's showdown with Notre Dame could make BYU a consensus top-five team with a victory.

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. Maryland (45-16) Next Week: at Indiana

Props to the Maryland defense for only allowing four catches for 93 yards and two touchdowns to Jeremiah Smith, who was coming off back-to-back 200-yard receiving games against Illinois and Iowa.

With a 31-10 lead at halftime, the Buckeyes were comfortably in control throughout the game, though it was not the cleanest performance from quarterback Julian Sayin, who threw an interception and lost a fumble. He still finished with 242 yards and four touchdown passes on only 13 completions.

Running back Bo Jackson had season highs in carries (23), rushing yards (107) and rushing touchdowns (2), helping to take some of the pressure off Sayin and the passing game, and that was more than enough to overwhelm the Maryland defense.

5. Alabama Crimson Tide (5-1, Previous Rank: 5)

Week 6 Result: LOSS vs. Georgia (17-20) Next Week: at Tennessee

A six-play, 31-yard drive and a five-play, 41-yard drive both ended in punts, and that ended up being the final two possessions of the game for the Crimson Tide. In between, Georgia kicked a 23-yard field goal to take the lead in an evenly matched game start to finish.

Keelon Russell had 185 passing yards and 41 rushing yards, but he accounted for just one touchdown as the Georgia defense bent but didn't break against Alabama's breakout star.

Next week's road game against Tennessee now takes on additional importance as they look to avoid a second loss.

4. Indiana Hoosiers (6-0, Previous Rank: 6)

Week 6 Result: WIN at Nebraska (20-17) Next Week: vs. Ohio State

Josh Hoover (12/22, 263 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) and Nick Marsh (6 catches, 187 yards, 2 TD) connected on a pair of fourth quarter touchdown strikes, helping the Hoosiers survive by far their toughest test of the year.

The running game managed just 65 yards on 22 carries, and they were 1-of-10 on third-down conversions en route to six punts.

However, the offense came up with a 65-yard touchdown drive when it mattered in the fourth quarter, and the second Hoover-to-Marsh scoring connection gave Indiana its first outright lead of the day with 7:13 remaining in the game.

3. Miami Hurricanes (5-0, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 6 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Florida State

A convincing 41-13 victory on the road against Clemson last week provided a smooth entry point into the Hurricanes bye week. Right now they look like the clear team to beat in the ACC, and should be favored in every remaining conference game.

A Nov. 7 game on the road against Notre Dame still looms large, but there's a viable path to the playoff field for both of those teams regardless of the outcome, and especially if the final score is close.

Darian Mensah (84.2 cmp%, 1,438 yards, 15 TD, 0 INT) and Malachi Toney (39 catches, 604 yards, 6 TD) have been two of the most productive players in the country, while the defense is allowing an FBS-low 9.8 points per game.

2. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (6-0, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 6 Result: WIN vs. Stanford (58-7) Next Week: at BYU

The Fighting Irish scored the first 44 points of the game and cruised to victory against an overmatched Stanford team that has now been outscored by a staggering 249-94 margin on the year, despite their two wins.

Notre Dame punted twice, but put points on the board in their other nine completed drives. CJ Carr threw for 181 yards and three touchdowns in an abbreviated outing, while Jonaz Walker (13 carries, 181 yards, 2 TD) and Nolan James Jr. (10 carries, 73 yards, 2 TD) led a rushing attack that finished with 361 yards and five touchdowns.

Wisconsin is a good team and North Carolina made things interesting a week ago, but next week's matchup on the road against BYU will be far and away the toughest test of the season so far in Notre Dame's quest to return to the College Football Playoff field.

1. Georgia Bulldogs (6-0, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 6 Result: WIN at Alabama (20-17) Next Week: vs. Auburn

After missing a 39-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter, Peyton Woodring was true on a 23-yard chip shot to cap off a 10-play, 84-yard drive with 5:25 remaining in the fourth quarter. That stood up as the game-winning score in a hard-fought matchup of two clear national championship contenders.

The Georgia defense forced a punt on the ensuing Alabama drive, and managed to run out the remainder of the clock on their possession to seal the victory.

The Bulldogs had 455 total yards, with Dwight Phillips Jr. (17 carries, 120 yards) anchoring a rushing attack that finished with 206 yards on 39 carries. Gunner Stockton threw for 249 yards and a touchdown while completing 18 of 22 attempts.

articles.body:
Celtic will look to bounce back from their first league defeat of the season in the final match before the international break as they prepare for a showdown against Motherwell on Sunday in their next Scottish Premiership match.

Motherwell vs Celtic – Match preview and team news

Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson reported no fresh concerns from international duty but must navigate an extensive preexisting injury list at Fir Park.

The Steelmen are definitely without defender Dylan Williams, who sustained a fresh hamstring injury, while forward Regan Charles-Cook is not yet ready to return despite stepping up his rehabilitation.

They join a lengthy casualty list featuring Paul McGinn, Jordan McGhee, Callum Hendry, Johnny Koutroumbis, and Oscar Priestman.

After struggling for offensive productivity and scoring only one goal during a three-match losing streak, Johansson may shuffle his attacking options to revitalize the frontline.

Wide threat Tawanda Maswanhise is anticipated to spearhead the attack, heavily supported by creative midfielders Alex Lowry and Ibrahim Said as the home side seeks a crucial breakthrough against the champions.

Manager Martin O'Neill is expected to make a significant tactical adjustment, reverting Celtic to a traditional 4-2-3-1 formation with a standard four-man defense after an unsuccessful back-three trial against Rangers.

On the injury front, the Hoops receive a massive psychological boost with winger Jota returning to full training and potentially the matchday squad following a long-term knee injury.

However, the league leaders will still be missing several key figures. Right-back Alistair Johnston remains sidelined with a hamstring issue alongside Callum Osmand (ankle) and Yang Hyun-jun (hamstring), ensuring Colby Donovan keeps his spot at right-back.

Furthermore, center-back Cameron Carter-Vickers faces a late fitness assessment. Adding to O'Neill's selection dilemmas, Swedish winger Benjamin Nygren remains a primary doubt for the starting lineup after contracting a virus during the international break.

Celtic started their league campaign flawlessly with six consecutive victories, including dominant wins over Aberdeen and Kilmarnock. However, the league leaders entered the international break in a worrying slump, enduring three consecutive losses across all competitions. They suffered a heavy 3-0 League Cup exit to rivals Rangers, a 3-1 Europa League phase loss to Ferencváros, and a narrow 1-0 Premiership defeat to Rangers just before the break.

Motherwell: Paulsen; Sparrow, Girdwood-Reich, Moormann, Longelo; Fadinger, Hodge; Seb Palmer-Houlden, Alex Lowry, Ibrahim Said; Maswanhise

Celtic: Sinisalo; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Trusty, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; Hassan, Tounekti, Duran; Hogh

The Scottish Premiership match between Motherwell and Celtic will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football and Sky Sports Ultra HDR in the UK.

articles.title: Georgia deserves credit for gutsy win over Alabama, but Crimson Tide QB Keelon Russell has us hoping for a rematch
articles.summary: Georgia won the battle, but because of the electric Alabama quarterback who so graciously accepted his defeat Saturday night, Alabama might be better positio...
articles.body:
TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — The controversy over an uncalled pass interference penalty had dissolved into the night, a subdued version of "Dixieland Delight" had been played inside Bryant-Denny Stadium and Georgia had kneeled out the final two minutes of a 20-17 victory that cemented the Bulldogs as the nation's new No. 1 team .

Then, amidst the mass of bodies lingering at midfield, an Alabama player wearing No. 12 stood off to the side as an ABC camera crew interviewed Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton.

It was his counterpart, Alabama's emerging superstar Keelon Russell.

Russell waited patiently for a couple minutes as Stockton finished, long after most of his Alabama teammates had made a beeline for the locker room. Then, once the cameras were clear, Russell approached Stockton for a handshake and a congratulatory embrace. After more than three intense hours on opposite sidelines, it was the first time they had ever met face-to-face.

"He was awesome," Stockton said. "I've tried to do better with that, trying to go shake the other quarterback's hand no matter what. Seeing that at a younger age is pretty special."

Special just like this game. Just like this rivalry. Just like this entire, out-of-control college football season where it seems like every weekend is both a revelation and a contradiction.

So what do we make of a game so close, filled with so much emotion and played on the edge of brutality to the point where Georgia coach Kirby Smart came to his postgame press conference talking like a philosophy professor?

Here's one possible takeaway: Georgia won the battle, but because of the quarterback who so graciously accepted his defeat Saturday night, Alabama might be better positioned to win the war.

"There's no such thing as containing Russell," an exhausted Smart said after his defense survived and advanced to 6-0, knowing there will likely be a second meeting with far more significance somewhere down the line. "That kid is an elite athlete, an elite player. Hopefully we affected him some tonight, and he didn't have some of the numbers he's had [previously]. But he's going to be hell in this league for two years."

Indeed, if you can reduce this game to a box score, Georgia probably did as well as anyone could hope for against Russell: 16-of-30 passing for 185 yards and a touchdown. Including the four times Georgia sacked him, Russell netted only 41 rushing yards on nine attempts.

But the eye test told a different story. As good as Georgia's defense is — and make no mistake, it's arguably as elite as it was during the Bulldogs' championship runs in 2021 and 2022 — there were moments when Russell found the tiniest sliver of space and looked like a video game quarterback after someone smashed the turbo button.

He is breathtaking. He is frightening. And if these teams meet in December or January in a game where the loser goes home, are you really prepared to bet against that guy with a couple more months of experience under his belt?

Go ahead and start the debate. Would you rather have Stockton, the gritty, steady veteran who doesn't have the world's highest ceiling but usually seems to make the play Georgia needs exactly when they need it? Or, in a one-and-done playoff setting, would you rather have the electric, unlimited upside of a quarterback who you can look at and wonder at this early stage of development if he one day might be one of the greats?

Smart has his answer. He also has no choice.

"It's a deal that you get better with experience," he said of Stockton, who rebounded from an early tipped pass interception from his own 25-yard line to finish 18-of-22 for 249 yards. "He doesn't let things fester and affect him.

"I've been in a bunch of those with them and they all seem similar. Physical game, back and forth, critical calls, critical situations. You can go back and look at hundreds of them. At the end of the day our quarterback played well enough to win and we scored enough points to win."

But anyone making an honest assessment of what happened Saturday has to acknowledge how close Russell came to pulling off his first legendary win in an Alabama uniform. With 3:28 left and Alabama driving to either tie or take the lead, Russell directed a rainbow toward the end zone in the direction of a streaking Rico Scott, who had beaten his defender down the sideline.

Before the pass arrived, safety KJ Bolden ran across the goal line and shoved Scott without playing the ball — a clear pass interference infraction. But no penalty was called, much to the dismay of the Alabama sideline. Russell got sacked on the next play to take Alabama out of field goal range, and the Crimson Tide never got the ball back.

"This can be a really hard place to play," Georgia receiver London Humphreys said. "You can get rattled if something doesn't go your way. But these guys just put their head down and they did what they had to do and executed it like our standard."

Did Georgia deserve to win the game? Absolutely. But did that no-call cost Alabama an outstanding shot to steal it? Also, yes.

And so it sets up the delicious potential for a second meeting somewhere down the line, and as Smart understands, college football has never been more week-to-week. You can't consistently dominate anymore, and you can tell the thought of playing more of these exhausts him.

"Humility is a week away as you saw today," Smart said, referring to Texas and LSU going down in big upsets.

Then he continued with something you don't hear much from Smart after a big game like this: Introspection.

He came into the league as a Nick Saban-coded football maniac whose sole purpose, it seemed, was to win Georgia's first national championship since 1980. Sometimes in those early years, Smart was so intense about it that it seemed like he froze in the biggest games. As he reaches his 50th year of life, though, with all the money and all the accomplishments he ever dreamed of, he is thinking about the bigger picture.

"I was talking to my mom earlier today and I've got perspective things," he said, raising the topic unprompted. "I'm going to be judged on my kids, my wife, my mom, what kind of man I am. And I look at that a lot more than what someone is going to say about a record against Alabama or against the SEC or national championships. That's not my motivation anymore. I'd rather make memories for my team and our kids and my coaching staff."

But when a follow-up question came and the reporter suggested that he isn't motivated to win championships anymore, he immediately shut that down.

"I'm motivated to win championships," he said. "I worked for Mark Richt and Bobby Bowden and it was never just about the wins and losses. It was about the young men you're growing. Hell yeah I want to win championships, but I have a lot more perspective to know there's a lot more important things in life than just that."

Georgia proved Saturday night it is good enough to do it. But it also saw the team — and particularly the quarterback — that might be good enough to prevent it.

articles.title: Notre Dame Having The Most Untalked-About 6-0 Season In Program History
articles.summary: Notre Dame would typically be the talk of the town, but this version seems to be flying under the radar. […]
articles.body:
Notre Dame would typically be the talk of the town, but this version seems to be flying under the radar.

Notre Dame football typically makes headlines week in and week out of the college football season.

But this year, the Fighting Irish have been flying under the radar when it comes to the national scene.

This week, Notre Dame absolutely dominated an overmatched Stanford team, 58-7. With the win, Marcus Freeman's group is now 6-0 ahead of a showdown with BYU on the road.

Fighting Irish Look The Part Of A National Title Contender

Despite the lack of talk, Notre Dame seems to have the pieces in place to make the College Football Playoff.

They had no trouble with Wisconsin or Rice to begin the season. A 17-point victory over Michigan State followed before besting Purdue on the road by 39.

Notre Dame got by a pesky North Carolina team that is playing better than ever.

CJ Carr has been exceptional at quarterback. Carr is completing 71 percent of his passes for almost 1,200 yards and 13 touchdowns. He has thrown just one interception on 124 attempts, adding three rushing TDs.

Jonaz Walton has been on fire running the football as of late. He is one of three players with over 228 yards, averaging almost six per carry.

Aneyas Williams leads with 266 and four TDs, as Nolan James, Jr. has 262 and three touchdowns. Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert have over 700 yards receiving and six scores.

Notre Dame's Schedule Features Just Three Hurdles This Season

In addition to this coming Saturday's showdown on the road at BYU, the Fighting Irish have just two other real hurdles. And both of those games will take place in South Bend, Indiana.

After playing Navy to close out October, Notre Dame will welcome in Miami. They host Boston College the following week and play a third straight home contest against SMU.

Syracuse is the season finale and possibly all that stands between the Fighting Irish and an undefeated season.

articles.title: Manchester City vs Liverpool: Latest City team news and predicted City starting lineup
articles.summary: At long last, Manchester City return to action today when they take on Liverpool at Anfield in their sixth Premier League match of the season. After an inter...
articles.body:
At long last, Manchester City return to action today when they take on Liverpool at Anfield in their sixth Premier League match of the season. After an international break that seemed to drag on forever and with the 115 verdict arriving during that time, football has felt secondary to outside events. Enzo Maresca's side will arrive at Anfield as the villains of the piece and a hostile reception will await them today.

Despite this, City will be looking to extend their winning run which currently sits at seven matches in all competitions. They'll take on a Liverpool side who are sitting seventh on the table with two wins and three draws in their opening five matches of the 2026-27 season. Although, Andoni Iraola's side haven't set the world alight with their performances. Manchester City enter today's match sitting top of the Premier League table and will have to put the outside noise aside if they are to pick up three points at Anfield today.

Here is the latest City injury and team news, along with my predicted Manchester City starting eleven for today's match.

Phil Foden will miss today's match due to suspension. The England international is serving the third game of the three-match ban he received for being sent off for violent conduct in Manchester City's 1-0 win over Manchester United. Foden is in line to return for Manchester City's next UEFA Champions League fixture against PSG at the Etihad Stadium.

Enzo Maresca has declared that Erling Haaland is fit and available for today's match. Erling Haaland did suffer from fatigue over the international break. He was afforded a few days' rest after playing four games for Norway over the international break. Haaland will take his place in the City lineup today.

The only other fitness concerns for Manchester City surround Antoine Semenyo and Nico O'Reilly. Semenyo withdrew from international duty with Ghana due to a swollen ankle. However, he has trained ahead of today's match. This indicates that Semenyo will be ready to go against Liverpool. Nico O'Reilly sustained an undisclosed injury and was sent home early from international duty. It remains to be seen if he is fit enough to play in today's match.

Outside of that, Enzo Maresca has a strong squad to choose from for today's game. It would be expected that Maresca will select his strongest possible lineup for today's match. Manchester City do face PSG on Wednesday night. However, today's match takes priority. It is a huge match for a multitude of reasons and as such, I expect Enzo Maresca to go with his strongest available starting lineup today.
